CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male with a past medical history of depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. He reports that he started feeling tired and short of breath 1 week ago after working in the yard. He believes he caught his first cold and it got worse. The patient denies coughing up anything, fevers, nausea or vomiting, diarrhea, or muscle aches or joint pain.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression. He notes that he has been taking barre classes to help him relax and thinks it is working. He also reports that he has been monitoring his sugar levels while at work during the week but not on weekends. He states that his diet has been good for the most part except for house parties and things like that.

The patient reports that he has been monitoring his blood pressure at home but not on weekends. He states that it has been under control and he is taking lisinopril as prescribed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers, chills, or weight loss.
• Respiratory: Endorses shortness of breath on exertion.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Musculoskeletal: Endorses joint pain.
• Neurological: Endorses fatigue.

Cardiovascular: Strong heart sounds without murmurs or gallops. No edema of the lower extremities.

- Medical Treatment: We will send a COVID-19 test to rule out COVID-19 as the cause of his symptoms today in office.

- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with depression but states he is doing well with this at this time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrea Roberts is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux who presents today for her annual exam. She has been walking like I told her to and exercising and doing yoga, and that has actually helped with her arthritis a lot, just the constant movement. She has not had any joint pain recently.

She is still taking methotrexate once weekly without any issues. She denies any issues with the medication.

She has been having palpitations. The last one she had was about a week ago. She notices that when she starts to get stressed, they start to flare up again. She has been trying meditation, trying running with her dog to try and relieve the stress but it has not really been working.

She cut out soda and that seemed to help, and the medication has been helping too. She has not had a flare up in over 5 months.

The patient endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fatigue, weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Endorses palpitations.
• Respiratory: Endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm at this time. Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard over the heart. No lower extremity edema.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Event monitor results show that she is in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pause. Autoimmune panel shows normal results.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Rheumatoid Arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: Her current methotrexate prescription is well tolerated without any issues.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications that have helped her manage her symptoms.
- Medical Treatment: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly as prescribed. If she needs a referral back to see the rheumatologist, let me know but I think everything seems stable now.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
2. Atrial Fibrillation.
- Medical Reasoning: We have seen her in and out of atrial fibrillation on event monitor previously today we saw an episode of conversion pause on event monitor today which we will review in more detail later today but I believe we should attempt to keep her in normal sinus rhythm at this point given her age we want to avoid anticoagulation if possible so I am going to refer her for cardiac ablation which will map out where that rhythm is coming from and burn it so it does not come back again today we also reviewed event monitor results which show she is in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pause today we will review these further later today but I believe this will be an effective treatment option for her at this point given she is young we want to avoid anticoagulation if possible so I am going to refer her for cardiac ablation which will map out where that rhythm is coming from and burn it so it does not come back again today we also reviewed event monitor results which show she is in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pause today we will review these further later today but I believe this will be an effective treatment option for her at this point given she is young we want to avoid anticoagulation if possible so I am going to refer her for cardiac ablation which will map out where that rhythm is coming from and burn it so it does not come back again today we also reviewed event monitor results which show she is in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pause today we will review these further later today but I believe this will be an effective treatment option for her at this point given she is young we want to avoid anticoagulation if possible so I am going to refer her for cardiac ablation which will map out where that rhythm is coming from and burn it so it does not come back again.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hyperglycemia.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and kidney transplant. He is here today for emergency room follow-up.

The patient was seen in the emergency room over the weekend due to elevated blood sugar. He was not staying on top of his blood sugar readings and felt woozy. His wife took him in for evaluation and he was treated as an outpatient.

The patient reports that he has been having trouble managing his diet lately. He states that he has been doing well during the week but not on the weekends when he is busy with social activities. He believes that stopping eating would improve his diet.

The patient reports that he is doing well with his immunosuppression medications following up with Dr. Reyes 3 weeks ago. His kidney function was good at that time.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression, but it has been a tough year and a half. He states that he finds relaxation in meditation and would like to continue this for a couple of months to see how it goes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath, lightheadedness or dizziness.
• Psychiatric: Reports depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Cardiovascular: Carotid bruits are absent. Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard in the past.
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally. 1+ edema in lower extremities.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Hemoglobin A1c: 8%.
• Fasting Glucose: 162.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Hyperglycemia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's elevated blood glucose level is consistent with hyperglycemia.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications to help manage blood glucose levels today.
- Medical Treatment: Increase Lantus insulin to 20 units at night starting immediately. Continue monitoring blood glucose levels and report back to me if they are elevated again.
- Additional Testing: Order hemoglobin A1c in a couple of months.

Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with depression, however, he is doing well with current strategies including meditation.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed alternative management options today including holding off on medication or therapy at this time and encouraging him to call me if needed.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current strategies including meditation at home for the next couple of months without medication or therapy at this time.
- Additional Testing: None required today.

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Nguyen is a 54-year-old male with a past medical history, significant for osteoporosis and multiple sclerosis who presents for an annual exam. He has been traveling all over the country. It's been kind of a stressful summer. He is adjusting to everything in the fall and so far it's been good, but he is having trouble sleeping. He has tried everything from melatonin to meditation to stretching out every morning when he gets up. Nothing really seems to help though.

In terms of his osteoporosis, he is currently taking Fosamax 1 tab per week. He denies any issues with his joints or any recent broken bones.

In terms of his multiple sclerosis, he last saw the neurologist 6 months ago and is taking the medication. He denies any additional weakness, including his right leg which seems to have improved.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fatigue.
• Neurological: Endorses insomnia.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or swelling.

- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing on medications as prescribed by his neurologist.
- Medical Treatment: Continue on medications as prescribed by his neurologist.

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Lawrence Walker is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history significant for type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux. He presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of shortness of breath.

The patient reports that he has noticed swelling in his legs. He believes this is due to going to house parties and eating salty foods. He feels lethargic. The patient endorses shortness of breath when he walks up a flight of stairs. He denies shortness of breath when he is just sitting here. The patient endorses discomfort when he wakes up in the morning and feels stiff. He also denies waking up acutely short of breath at night.

The patient reports that his blood sugars have been stable lately, but he has not been monitoring them as frequently as he should be due to busy weekends. He admits to consuming chocolate bars regularly.

The patient reports that his depression has been a challenging year and a half. He has tried natural solutions such as stretching outdoors every morning, but now he is looking for alternative options. The patient denies suicidal ideation.

The patient reports that his alcohol intake has been difficult during the holiday season, but he is doing better now.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Endorses dyspnea on exertion.
• Cardiovascular: Endorses orthopnea.
• Neurological: Denies headaches, confusion, or altered mental status.
• Psychiatric: Endorses depression.
• Gastrointestinal: Endorses dysphagia.

Neck: No jugular venous distension or carotid bruits present.

The patient reports that she has not taken any medication for her pain, but she did take ibuprofen which did not seem to help. She has also not applied ice or put a splint on her finger.

The patient rates her pain as a 7 out of 10. She denies any other injuries while skiing down the trail.

The patient reports that she has chronic constipation and takes MiraLAX which seems to help.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she had an appendectomy at age 7.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is a female who is currently single and lives alone.

note.assessment_and_plan:

Right index finger sprain.
• Medical Reasoning: The examination and radiographic findings are consistent with a sprain of the distal interphalangeal joint (DIP) joint of the right index finger.
• Patient Education and Counseling: The patient was counseled in regards to her diagnosis and treatment options.

• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Cheryl Ramirez is a 34-year-old female with a past medical history significant for hypertension, who presents today with back pain. She reports that she has been walking 30 minutes to an hour per day and all of a sudden her back just kind of seized up on her. She denies any trauma before that happened. She has been lifting more, probably around 3 times a week. She does not know if it was because she was doing deadlifts that day and then walked. She may have been using her back more than her legs.

The patient endorses right-sided lower back pain, which is equally bilateral. She denies any numbness, tingling, or weakness in her lower extremities.

The patient reports that she has been taking ibuprofen and applying heat to the area. Her blood pressure is well controlled at home.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers, chills, or weight loss.
• Musculoskeletal: Endorses right-sided lower back pain.
• Neurological: Denies numbness, tingling, or weakness in the lower extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS:
• Blood pressure well controlled.
• Respiratory: Auscultation of heart and lungs are unremarkable except for a grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur stable from previous exams.
• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the neck reveals no tenderness to palpation. Examination of the spine reveals right lateral lumbar spine pain to palpation and pain with flexion and extension as well as a negative straight leg raise.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Back x-ray obtained today, not yet reviewed; Labs: all within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Lumbar strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with right-sided lower back pain which is equally bilateral. Her examination reveals right lateral lumbar spine pain to palpation and pain with flexion and extension as well as a negative straight leg raise. Her x-ray shows good bony alignment without any obvious fracture which is not surprising based on her history.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the nature of her diagnosis with the patient today and advised her on treatment options including meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management as well as icing the area and applying heat sometimes as well. I also advised her to refer to physical therapy for strengthening exercises of her back so she can continue to work out and exercise without exacerbating the condition.
- Medical Treatment: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain management. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening exercises of her back.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure is well controlled at home with lisinopril 10 mg daily.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder and elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Jose James is a 64-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder and elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began 5 months ago when he fell going up stairs due to icy conditions. He reports constant pain in his left shoulder and elbow, which is present at all times. The pain is worse with lifting, and he has not been able to lift more than 15 or 20 pounds due to the pain. He has tried icing and stopping exercise, which has provided some relief but not enough for him to continue with his usual activities.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he was an office worker until he retired last year.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is married and enjoys walking with his wife.

MEDICAL HISTORY

The patient denies any history of numbness or tingling.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder and elbow pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the left shoulder reveals tenderness over the acromioclavicular joint space without warmth, erythema, or deformity. Positive Hawkins-Kennedy test and Neer's test. Normal proximal and distal upper extremity strength. Intact median radial ulnar sensation and abduction to 90 degrees.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Impingement syndrome of the left shoulder.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms began after a fall onto his outstretched left hand, which likely caused injury to his left shoulder. His symptoms are consistent with impingement syndrome of the left shoulder.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today, including physical therapy as well as cortisone injection if necessary.
• Medical Treatment: I have ordered a referral for Dr. Martha Rivera for physical therapy 2 days per week.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

• Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with a viral upper respiratory infection. Sinus infections often start out as viral infections and can become bacterial if left untreated.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the nature of his symptoms with the patient's mother today and advised her that we will monitor him closely for any signs of worsening symptoms such as a barking cough. • Special Tests: None today.
• Patient Agreements: The patient's mother understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acne.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents for a new visit with her mother for acne located on the face, which started about 2 years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which is somewhat helpful. There are no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain.

The patient denies any flare-ups with her periods. She states she gets a regular period and has been getting one for about 2 years. She notes that the biggest flare was when she started school sports in the fall due to all the sweating.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports no additional past medical history.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives with parents and sister. They have a dog, bird, and rabbits in the home. She is in the 7th grade and active in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing.
She wears sunscreen in the summer, SPF 30.
No additional family history.

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports using Persa-Gel.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Denies itching, bleeding or pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• General Examination: The patient appears well-developed and well-nourished for her age. Her vital signs are within normal limits today.
• Skin: Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythematous papules on the face primarily on the forehead and central cheeks and chin.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Acne.
• Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's current acne appears to be mild to moderate acne primarily comedonal with small inflammatory component. Her skin care routine has been somewhat helpful but not as effective as desired.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed her current skin care routine today. I advised her to wash her face with a mild cleanser each morning then apply a noncomedogenic moisturizer labeled SPF 30 or higher. In the evening she should wash her face with the same cleanser then allow it to dry before applying adapalene 0.1% cream in a thin layer to areas where she generally gets acne. She should start off using this a few nights per week then work up to using it every night if tolerated without any adverse effects such as dryness or irritation which may require wearing sunscreen when outside.
• Medical Treatment: We will start off with topical therapy first today by having her use adapalene 0.1% cream in a thin layer to areas where she generally gets acne at night starting off with just a few nights per week then working up to nightly use if tolerated without any adverse effects such as dryness or irritation which may require wearing sunscreen when outside if it is very expensive or not covered by insurance she can try different gel over-the-counter followed by Clean & Clear Persa-Gel in a thin layer or where she generally gets acne then noncomedogenic moisturizer.

Hematuria.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mrs. Kelly Wood is a pleasant 41-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for renal ultrasound due to hematuria. The patient reports that she has had bright red urine for the past 6 weeks, which she describes as the color of cherry Kool-Aid. She also reports that she has had episodes of dysuria and pain, which she rates an 8 out of 10 at the time. The patient states that she passed 2 small stones last week after scheduling this appointment. She denies flank pain or lower back tenderness at this time.

The patient is a chronic urolithiasis patient and notes that she drinks more Mountain Dew than water. She is currently taking Alavert 10 mg tablet once daily and denies any drug allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss, fevers, chills.
• Genitourinary: Reports hematuria, dysuria, pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Examination: Urine dipstick today negative for leukocytes, nitrates, protein, ketone, bilirubin and glucose. Color yellow and clear with urobilinogen 0.2 EU/dL and pH 5.5 and specific gravity 1.020. There is a trace amount of blood in the urine and intact.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Urine dipstick today.
Color yellow and clear.
Appearance clear.
Leukocytes negative.
Nitrates negative.
Protein negative.
Ketone negative.
Bilirubin negative.
Glucose negative.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Hematuria.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's hematuria was due to kidney stones which were successfully passed last week. She still has one stone in her left kidney but it's not obstructing or causing pain at this time so I do not recommend any surgical intervention at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the formation of kidney stones can not be attributed to a particular cause but several factors increase the risk such as dehydration, family history, certain foods, digestive tract disease and certain medical conditions. I advised her to drink about half of her body weight in ounces of water a day if she weighs 250 pounds that would be 125 ounces of water a day and avoid drinking sugary drinks like Mountain Dew. I also advised her to avoid food rich in sodium oxalate and animal protein such as salty processed food because they are high in sodium ideally consume less than 1000 milligrams of sodium per day reduce the amount of beef poultry fish pork. We discussed what oxalate is it's an organic acid found in plants when digested it binds to minerals that stones are formed from foods like spinach chocolate beets rhubarb soy products.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Alavert 10 mg tablet once daily as prescribed.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Sanchez is a pleasant 58-year-old female who presents today for a follow-up status post mitral valve repair performed on 8/3/2020. She reports that she is doing well from a cardiac standpoint. She notes that she was having a rough time before surgery, but she thinks she is overall pretty good now though.

The patient denies any new symptoms at this time. She does report that she is still getting some chest pains sometimes and her breathing gets shallow. However, she states that if she feels like that when exerting herself, she slows down a bit which helps, and then when she goes back to it later, she can usually finish whatever she was doing.

She adds that these episodes seem to last only a few minutes and then they disappear for a couple of weeks. When these episodes occur, the patient just takes the day nice and slow and does not push herself.

The patient reports that she has been trying to keep up with her medications regularly. She states that there are a lot of extra pills now but has a reminder app so she does pretty well. The patient confirms taking Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 40 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily.

She denies any side effects from the medications at this time. The patient notes that the Atenolol makes her irritable in the beginning but states that it does not seem to bother her as much now.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea on exertion.
• Cardiovascular: Endorses chest pain.
• Neurological: Denies fatigue.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Head and Neck: No JVD detected in neck examination. Lateral neck flexion reveals no JVD.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
ECG taken on 12/26/2020 reveals atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly compared to the previous study there are no significant changes.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Status post mitral valve repair.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well from a cardiac standpoint at this time. Her ECG taken today shows atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response but no significant changes compared to the previous study.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications with the patient today including regular exercise which will certainly help improve her symptoms.
• Medical Treatment: Continue Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 40 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily as prescribed by the physician.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Judy Gomez is a 61-year-old female who presents today for ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis. She reports that she has been doing well since her last visit, and she has been able to discontinue prednisone 1 mg daily. She notes that she only takes an extra dose when she has a day off and is moving around a lot, which tends to hurt her feet more. She estimates that this occurs once a week.

The patient reports that methotrexate has helped with her joint pain. She notes that she did not take it for one week when she received her COVID-19 vaccination due to concerns about efficacy, but after taking it again the following week, she felt absolutely horrible until then. The patient called the hotline and was advised to continue taking the medication.

The patient denies any recent weight loss or fevers.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports joint pain in the knees and feet.
Skin: Denies any new or worsening psoriasis.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MS GOMEZ is a pleasant 61-year-old female in no acute distress. Examination of the skin reveals ridges in nails consistent with psoriasis.
Examination of the joints reveals mild stiffness in the knees and feet bilaterally with some pain on palpation. Range of motion is good in both knees bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.
• Continue methotrexate as prescribed.
• Discontinue prednisone 1 mg daily today and monitor for any signs of rebound effect or worsening symptoms.
• Schedule blood work for review in 3 months.

Newly diagnosed heart murmur.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diana Scott is a pleasant 100-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for a new patient evaluation. The patient reports that she was recently diagnosed with a heart murmur by her primary care physician. She states that she is asymptomatic, but does have severe leg pain. She denies chest pain or shortness of breath. The patient reports that she has been taking pain medication for her leg pain.

The patient states that she has been using a walker to ambulate due to fatigue. She notes that her fatigue is likely due to her medications. The patient denies any fevers, chills, or other symptoms.

The patient reports that she has had several surgeries in the past, but does not recall the specifics of each procedure.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that her son had a myocardial infarction. Her brother had a stroke and has diabetes. Her older sister has an unknown heart problem, and family members are positive for heart disease.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is currently taking Levothyroxine, Lisinopril, Simvastatin 20 mg, Meclizine, and Amlodipine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain over the past year.
• Cardiovascular: Endorses severe leg pain.
• Neurological: Endorses lightheadedness and dizziness.
note.objective_exam:

• Constitutional: Elderly in no acute distress.
• Cardiovascular: Normal S1 and S2 is preserved with a normal rate and regular rhythm. There is a 4/6 systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Low back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Bryan Brooks is a pleasant 39-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of low back pain. The onset of his pain began 2 hours ago when he was raking leaves in his yard. He denies any prior history of similar episodes. He states that he has not been doing any physical activity lately. His pain is worse with standing and bending, but improves with sitting and applying heat. He denies any radiation of pain to his right lower extremity.

The patient reports that he has been doing yard work for the past 3 years, but this is the first time he has experienced pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he had an episode of low back pain 3 years ago, which resolved after a day.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he normally does not engage in physical activity. His partner is also present today and reports that he is experiencing similar symptoms when standing up.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the right lower extremity reveals normal dorsiflexion and pulses are equal in all extremities. There is some tingling sensation in the right leg.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of the low back were obtained today and reviewed in office today. They are unremarkable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Low back strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms began after raking leaves in his yard, which suggests a possible mechanical cause for his current symptoms. His examination reveals some pain with flexion, but no radiation to his right lower extremity.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of his condition with him today and advised him to rest it at home.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed meloxicam for him to take as needed for pain relief. I have also prescribed physical therapy to help him get back into shape and improve his flexibility and strength.
- Additional Testing: We will follow up in 2 weeks if his symptoms do not improve at which point we will order an MRI if necessary.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that he has had the ulcer for approximately 2 months and it has recently become red and is draining. He states that he believes he may have gotten it from walking barefoot on the beach.

The patient denies any trauma to his foot at the onset of the ulcer. He was seen by his primary care physician (PCP) prior to coming to see us today, who prescribed him medication for his ulcer. The patient states that he did not pick up the medication from the pharmacy yet.

The patient reports that his diabetes is not well controlled. He states that he takes his medication but does not check his blood sugar levels regularly. His last A1C was approximately 10, which is high.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports history of walking barefoot on the beach.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right foot pain and swelling.
Skin: Reports redness and drainage from right foot ulcer.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Examination: Vital signs are within normal limits. No fever present.
Neurological: Examination of bilateral lower extremities reveals normal sensation to light touch in all extremities. No clubbing or cyanosis noted.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray of right foot taken prior to today's visit shows no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Diabetic Foot Ulcer.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's diabetes is likely contributing to his non-healing right foot ulcer due to poor glycemic control.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed with the patient how his diabetes is likely contributing to his non-healing right foot ulcer due to poor glycemic control. We also discussed with him how wearing a shoe can help reduce pressure on his foot and promote healing.
- Medical Treatment: We ordered an ankle brachial index (ABI) study today to determine if there is adequate blood flow in his right lower extremity. We also performed a debridement today, which will remove some of the dead tissue from the ulcer site. I have also prescribed clindamycin 400 mg twice daily for 7 days, which will help treat any current infection present at this time. I have also ordered a shoe for him to wear while this is happening as wearing regular shoes can irritate this area further and hinder healing.
- Additional Testing: An ABI study will be ordered today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began 2 days ago when she slipped and fell on her left ankle. She states that she was walking to her car and slipped on ice. She denies any bleeding from the ankle. The patient reports that she was able to get up after the fall but it was very sore and started swelling and quite a bit of pain, making it hard to walk. She has tried ibuprofen, ice, and elevation which have provided some relief.

The patient denies any pain above her ankle, stating that it is mostly just the outside of her ankle. She denies any calf or lower leg pain or knee pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she has type 2 diabetes and hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is taking metformin for diabetes management. Her blood sugars have been stable lately. She states that she has been cutting back on sweets and sugars and exercising regularly.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she is taking metformin for diabetes management and Norvasc for hypertension.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left ankle pain.
Neurological: Denies calf or lower leg pain or knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

NECK EXAM: No bruits present in the neck. Lungs are clear bilaterally. Heart exam is normal with a grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from previous exams, which is not concerning for new pathology.
Belly Exam: Normal abdominal examination without masses, tenderness, or guarding.
ANKLE EXAM: There is tenderness over the lateral malleolus and tenderness over the 5th metatarsal bone. There is swelling, redness, and some pain with valgus stressing of the ankle as well. Normal sensation to light touch distally in all toes bilaterally with normal pulses.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray of the left ankle will be ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Ankle sprain with possible fracture.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with left ankle pain after a fall onto her outstretched left foot 2 days ago. Her examination reveals tenderness over the lateral malleolus and 5th metatarsal bone as well as swelling, redness, and some pain with valgus stressing of her ankle bilaterally. These findings are concerning for an ankle sprain but also possible fracture given her symptoms at this point in time.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options today including an x-ray of her left ankle which will be ordered today as well as an air splint which we placed on her today as well as crutches until we receive the x-ray results back in order to avoid weight bearing at this time due to concern for fracture at this point in time I also advised her to continue with ibuprofen 500 mg twice daily for pain control keep elevated apply ice to it I think those are all good things if there is no fracture then we will try partial weight bearing once we receive the x-ray results back from radiology at this point in time I also advised her to continue exercising as well as continuing with metformin for diabetes management as well as continuing Norvasc for hypertension.

Neck pain.

The patient is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of neck pain. He reports that he was in a car accident 1 week ago when he was struck from behind and his neck went forward and his head went forward quickly. He has been experiencing neck pain ever since. The pain is located in the back of his neck and is rated 7/10 in severity. The pain is not constant but worsens with movement of his head. He denies any improvement with ibuprofen, which he has been taking for 5/10 relief.

The patient reports that he played football years ago without any neck issues.

The patient reports that he played football years ago without any neck issues.

The patient reports that he takes ibuprofen as needed.
note.objective_exam:

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

After reviewing the patient's examination and radiographic findings today, I have had a lengthy discussion with him regarding his current symptoms.
Neck strain.
- Medical Treatment: I am going to start him on Motrin 600 mg every 6-8 hours as needed for anti-inflammatory purposes. I am also going to prescribe Flexeril 10 mg every 12 hours as needed for muscle relaxation.
- Conservative Management: I want him to try to be conservative with how he moves about and avoid straining his neck anymore.
- Imaging: We are going to order an MRI just because we did not have him go to the hospital or anything like that. This will help us rule out a concussion or nerve impingement.
- Referral: I am going to refer him to either physical rehab or a chiropractor once we get the results of the MRI just to make sure there isn't any nerve impingement or other issues.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Bobby Flores is a pleasant 56-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder pain. The onset of his symptoms began 2 weeks ago when he was doing yard work. He notes that he was sore all over the next couple of days but his right shoulder just keeps on bothering him and it keeps it sore and it hasn’t been going away. He denies any numbness in his arm or hands.

The patient reports that he has had some issues with his right shoulder before, as he hurt that same shoulder playing baseball when he was younger. He states that this is the first time he has had issues with his right shoulder, but it does not feel like it is in the rotator cuff. He describes the pain as being on the outside and tender to palpation when he raises his arm up.

The patient states that there is no restriction with his arm, but he definitely feels some pain on the outside of it. He notes that his pain comes and goes, but whenever he moves it then he can definitely feel some pain. He also notes that at night, his pain does bother him as well because he sleeps on that side.

The patient reports that he has been taking Advil and icing as much as possible for pain relief. This has helped a little bit, but it still feels sore to touch.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of right shoulder pain when he was younger while playing baseball.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No tenderness to palpation or movement.
Right Shoulder: Limited active and passive range of motion. There is tenderness at the great tuberosity of the humerus. No tenderness at the sternoclavicular or acro acromioclavicular joints. Good hand grip.
Neurovascular: Capillary refill is less than 3 seconds bilaterally. Sensation to light touch is intact bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

3 views of the right shoulder were obtained today and reviewed in office today. There is no fracture.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Left Shoulder Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff rotator cuff tendinopathy.
- Additional Testing: We will order an MRI due to previous history of injury.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Tylenol for 6-8 weeks if symptoms do not improve we can consider steroid injection of the shoulder.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed treatment options with him today including physical therapy for 6-8 weeks which should be very successful in treating this condition if not we can consider steroid injection which could provide some relief.
2. Bilateral Foot Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s symptoms are most likely due to dehydration.
- Additional Testing: We will try Epsom salts soaking if symptoms do not improve we may start adding water supplements.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mark Jackson is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of his pain began 3 weeks ago when he started playing tennis again. He notes that his pain is located on the outside of his elbow and is worse with movement and better with rest. He denies any trauma to the area. The patient has tried taking Tylenol and ibuprofen, but they do not provide relief. He also tried icing his elbow, but it did not help.

The patient reports that he has been playing tennis regularly again, which he notes was good for his diabetes, but he believes he may be overdoing it a bit.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of type 2 diabetes.
He also reports a history of mild intermittent asthma.
He had a cholecystectomy 10 years ago by Dr. Nelson.
He is allergic to penicillin.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is currently taking metformin 500 mg twice daily, Flovent twice daily, and albuterol as needed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain. Denies left elbow pain or right shoulder pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior exam. Normal cardiovascular exam otherwise.
MSK: Examination of the right elbow reveals moderate lateral epicondylar tenderness. Passive range of motion is painful with full extension but normal with flexion. Mild pain with resisted wrist extension bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow today shows no acute fracture or other bony abnormality. No malalignment or joint effusion noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute lateral epicondylitis of the right elbow.
- Medical Reasoning: This is due to overuse likely from increased tennis activity which normally would be good but maybe we are overdoing it a little bit.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the nature of this condition with the patient in detail today and explained that rest, ice, bracing, and anti-inflammatory medication will help alleviate symptoms.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed an orthotics brace for his right forearm which will be provided by our nurse before discharge today. I have also prescribed Ultram 50 mg once per day which should help with pain management at this time.
- Additional Testing: We will reevaluate in 4 weeks at which time we will consider additional imaging if needed or possibly refer him to physical therapy depending on how he is doing at that time.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus uncontrolled.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood sugar levels are elevated at this time and need to be brought under control through dietary modifications and medication adjustments as necessary.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed dietary modifications with him in detail today including limiting candy consumption as well as increasing physical activity such as tennis in moderation to help improve blood sugar control. I also advised him to check his blood sugar twice daily for the next two weeks so we can make additional adjustments if necessary at that time.
- Medical Treatment: We will increase his metformin dose to 1000 mg twice per day starting immediately today. We will also order a hemoglobin A1c level, CBC blood test, and chem-12 blood test today so we can review these results together in follow-up.

RESULTS

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kenneth King is a pleasant 44-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began 5 days ago when he was skiing on Lake Martin. He states that he twisted his right knee when he landed from a jump and it has been hurting him ever since. He denies any popping or feeling of anything pop when he sustained the injury. He was able to get out of the water by himself but notes that climbing up and squatting or bending is very sore. He has never injured this knee before.

The patient reports that he is a frequent water skier and tries to go every weekend when they can. He denies any numbness or tingling in his foot at this time.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he had a tonsillectomy.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is married and enjoys outdoor activities, particularly skiing.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is currently taking lisinopril 20 mg once daily for hypertension.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain, swelling, and ecchymosis. Denies numbness or tingling in the foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: No lymphadenopathy.
• Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs.
• Lung: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals ecchymosis, edema, effusion present. There is pain to palpation over the medial aspect of the knee. Range of motion is decreased bilaterally with pain on movement. Negative varus and valgus testing, negative Lachman sign.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right medial collateral ligament strain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to his right medial collateral ligament when he twisted his knee while skiing on Lake Martin 5 days ago. His examination today reveals ecchymosis, edema, effusion present over the medial aspect of his right knee with pain to palpation over this area as well as decreased range of motion bilaterally with pain on movement. His Lachman sign was negative which makes me think that there was no significant anterior translation at the time of injury but I do think there was some degree of valgus stress at the time of injury which would have caused some degree of ligamentous laxity in this area.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him what we discussed today and explained my plan in detail including x-ray ordering for further evaluation as well as referral to physical therapy for strengthening exercises around his knees so that he does not have another injury in this area.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an x-ray of his right knee today for further evaluation as well as prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily which will help reduce swelling and pain in this area as well as refer him to physical therapy for strengthening exercises around his knees so that he does not have another injury in this area.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient has been compliant with lisinopril 20 mg once daily for hypertension but notes that his blood pressure has been elevated at home most days with readings ranging from 125/80 which is consistent with uncontrolled hypertension at this point in time given his age and medical history I believe we need to get a lipid panel ordered today so we can evaluate if there are any other contributing factors such as dyslipidemia contributing to his elevated blood pressure level at home today.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him what we discussed today including lifestyle modifications such as diet changes, weight loss if necessary, increased physical activity, stress reduction techniques such as meditation or yoga etc., medication adherence including taking lisinopril daily without exception, regular follow-up appointments with me every 3 months until blood pressure levels are controlled at goal levels per AHA guidelines.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 20 mg once daily; order lipid panel.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Incidental finding of a right upper lobe lung nodule.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a pleasant 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of an incidental finding of a right upper lobe lung nodule. He reports that he has been experiencing a cough for approximately 3 months. He states that he first noticed the cough when he was loading horses and then it started to get worse. He believes that he got a cold at that time and his cough resolved. The patient denies any previous history of lung infections or pneumonia.

The patient reports that he is an avid biker and exercises regularly. He states that he prefers riding on the trails rather than on the road.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he has a history of rheumatoid arthritis, which is currently well controlled with methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly. He denies any recent flares.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he was a previous smoker, but stopped smoking approximately 7 years ago.

FAMILY HISTORY

The patient reports that his mother had breast cancer, but she is doing well now. He denies any family history of lung cancer or other malignancies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea on exertion, productive cough, hemoptysis.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies pain or shortness of breath.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi are appreciated.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• CT scan of chest demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Incidental finding of right upper lobe lung nodule.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for the evaluation of an incidental finding of a right upper lobe lung nodule on CT scan from his primary care physician. His symptoms began approximately 3 months ago when he noticed a persistent cough while loading horses. The patient denies any previous history of lung infections or pneumonia.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I explained to the patient in detail what we discussed today and answered all his questions to his satisfaction.
• Medical Treatment: I have ordered pulmonary function testing (PFT) to obtain baseline values for his lung function. I have also scheduled a PET CT scan to determine if this nodule is metabolically active (i.e., lights up). We will discuss these results in more detail at my next visit with him.
• Additional Testing: PET CT scan ordered due to his smoking history and presence of this nodule.
• Surgical Treatment: If this is found to be cancerous, we will proceed with video-assisted thoracoscopy (VATS) removal with general anesthesia. This will involve making 3 small incisions on the side of his right chest and removing the nodule along with a small portion of his lung tissue. We will place a chest tube in place post-operatively until it can be removed bedside on day 2 post-op and discharge him home on day 3 post-op.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today for the evaluation of difficulty swallowing. The onset of his symptoms began 4 to 5 weeks ago. He describes that he has noticed something is always stuck in his throat and he has to wash it down on occasion. He denies ever fully choking but admits that he has thought about potentially choking. He notes that the sensation is more pronounced when he swallows solids, such as a bite of a sandwich, rather than liquids. He denies any weight loss or changes in his weight at this time.

The patient reports that he has noticed no blood in his stool or vomit, and denies any chest pain or shortness of breath with this symptom.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of diabetes and hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is not taking his blood glucose levels regularly, but estimates that he checks them approximately 80% of the time. His blood glucose levels are reportedly within the target range on most occasions.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking metformin 500 mg twice daily and Norvasc.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss.
• Digestive: Denies hematemesis, melena, abdominal pain.
• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: No swelling or masses present. Thyroid feels normal to palpation. No lymphadenopathy.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Difficulty swallowing.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with esophageal narrowing or stricture causing dysphagia. His hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 7.4 previously but has been improved with dietary modifications and adherence to medication regimen.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of his symptoms with him today and advised him to chew his food frequently when eating solid foods to prevent them from getting stuck in the esophagus. I also recommended that he contact my office if he experiences worsening symptoms or if they do not improve with these measures.
- Medical Treatment: I am going to refer him for gastroenterology for further evaluation and possible dilation of the esophagus if necessary. I am also going to prescribe Prilosec 20 mg once daily for gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) as it can exacerbate dysphagia in some patients.
• Diabetes Mellitus Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: His hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 7.4 previously but has been improved with dietary modifications and adherence to medication regimen.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of his symptoms with him today and advised him to continue adhering to his current medication regimen as prescribed by me today. We will repeat his hemoglobin A1c on my next visit if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: Continue metformin as prescribed by me today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain and instability.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain and instability. The onset of his symptoms began when he was playing basketball with his son. He states that he was going for a shot and landed awkwardly, rolling and twisting his right ankle. He describes the pain as being on the outside of his ankle, which is bruised up and swollen. He reports that he has been having trouble walking due to the pain and instability in his right ankle.

The patient reports that he recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine, but he does not want to disrupt this due to the current nature of his symptoms.

PAST HISTORY

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and instability.
Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient works from home. Plans to coach his son’s basketball team in 04/2022.
Patient enjoys working out and recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right ankle reveals swelling on the lateral side. There is exquisite tenderness over the lateral aspect of the ankle. There is tenderness over the medial deltoid region. Brisk capillary refill is present without any signs of epidermolysis or malalignment.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture.
1. Medical Treatment: Prescribe meloxicam for pain management.
2. Conservative Management: Ice, elevate, non-weight bearing with crutches for 3 months.
3. Surgical Intervention: Recommended due to location of fracture; will discuss further at length today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Facial pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of facial pain. He reports that he has had right-sided facial pain for approximately 2 months. The pain is described as stabbing and shooting in nature, and it is usually located in the right cheek bone area. He states that the pain is sometimes accompanied by heat, and he believes this may be triggered by cold temperatures or certain sensory stimuli. The patient denies any left-sided facial pain or weakness. He also denies any sensory loss, numbness, or tingling in the right cheek. His teeth are symmetric.

The patient reports that he has tried ibuprofen and Motrin without relief. He has also applied Tiger Balm to the area without success. He was referred to his family doctor who advised him to see a neurosurgeon.

PAST HISTORY

The patient denies any history of multiple sclerosis or brain tumors.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient denies any specific allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Eyes: Extraocular movements are intact in all directions. Vision is unchanged bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the head was reviewed today in office and it appears to have small blood vessel abutting and possibly pinching the trigeminal nerve. This may be consistent with trigeminal neuralgia.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Trigeminal neuralgia.
- Medical Treatment: We will start with Tegretol as first line treatment due to its efficacy in reducing excitability of the nerve and its relatively favorable side effect profile compared to Gabapentin.
- Additional Testing: Genetic testing will be ordered to assess for Eustachian tube dysfunction as this can be a predisposing factor for medication side effects.
- Patient Education and Counseling: The patient will be counseled on potential side effects of Tegretol including memory loss, tingling, imbalance, dermatologic reactions, and Eustachian tube dysfunction.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

The patient reports that she is otherwise healthy.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Rebecca Thompson is a 27-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began 1 month ago when she started swimming more regularly. She has been swimming freestyle with her legs kicking straight out, but she has noticed that her symptoms started after 2 laps. She was able to swim 10 laps without any pain initially, but now she can only complete 2 laps before her pain starts. She denies any history of injury.

The patient reports that she has been doing well with her chronic back pain, which comes and goes. She denies any lower extremity pain or weakness.

The patient reports that she has been doing well with her depression, and that it has been stable for the past few months. She is currently taking medication for depression and therapy.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies lower extremity weakness or numbness.
Psychiatric: Reports stable depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Examination of the right knee: No swelling in the joint. Range of motion is slightly limited due to pain with patellar inhibition. Pain on palpation over the patella.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was reviewed today and shows no evidence of fracture or dislocation. The x-ray is otherwise unremarkable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Chondromalacia of the patella.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with chondromalacia of the patella, which is a common cause of knee pain in athletes who participate in high-impact sports such as swimming.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with the patient that this is likely due to overuse from swimming and advised her to avoid activities that put extra pressure on her knees for a couple weeks until this improves.
- Medical Treatment: I prescribed ibuprofen 600 mg four times a day with food, as well as recommend straight leg raising exercises to strengthen her quadriceps muscle.
- Additional Testing: X-ray was reviewed today and shows no evidence of fracture or dislocation.
2. Chronic back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's chronic back pain has been well controlled at this time, but if it flares up again, she should contact me for further evaluation and treatment options.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to continue swimming as long as it does not flare up again at this time.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current medication for depression at this time; no changes are needed at this point regarding carpal tunnel release status.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant 32-year-old female who presents for a return visit for IBS with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was last seen in August 2019 with flares of abdominal pain, who was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome that was treated with Bentyl.

The patient reports that she has been going out to eat on Friday nights and Saturday nights and has had some spicy foods or spicy shrimp. She states that her gut does not like it at all. The patient also reports that she has been getting both lower belly cramps and upper belly nausea.

The patient states that she is starting to notice it is between 2-3 times a day on normal days. Her stools are formed. She also reports that after she has gone out drinking with friends, she tends to have more diarrhea. The patient feels it is the food or alcohol or both.

She usually goes to Fridays restaurant and always eats pasta, the chicken alfredo. She normally does not have any issues with this but notes that pasta can make her bloated. Grilled chicken is usually okay but the alfredo sauce is higher in fat and contains dairy. The patient prefers Patron but will only get brown liquor if available.

On days when she does not eat out or drink, her bowel movements are regular. However, when it flares up, it might not be as bad.

The patient denies any luck using the fiber like Citrucel regularly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Digestive: Reports diarrhea, nausea, vomiting.
• Psychiatric: Denies depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Constitutional: Alert and cooperative in no acute distress.
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes or rales heard.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant female with IBS and functional abdominal pain aggravated by high stress, poor eating habits, and poor sleeping habits.
I have encouraged dietary and lifestyle modifications as well as starting a neuromodulator such as Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for IBS.
She can use Bentyl 20 mg as needed 30-45 minutes prior to eating out at a restaurant. She can also use Zofran if needed however I have encouraged her to reduce greasy and fatty foods and alcohol consumption.
I have asked her to follow up in one month by emailing over MyChart regarding any side effects or issues or if adjustments are needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Adult hydrocephalus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Christopher Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns in follow-up for adult hydrocephalus. This is his first visit since undergoing shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020.

The patient was status post shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020, and was placed with a Medtronic Strata programmable shunt in the ventricular peritoneal configuration at level 2.0.

The patient reports that he has been doing much better since his shunt surgery. He states that his walking has improved and he is now able to walk to the dining room just fine. However, he still has times where he needs assistance. His bladder control did improve after surgery but now seems to have leveled out and he is wearing diapers.

The patient denies any headaches or pain from the shunt. He also denies any pain in his abdomen.

Regarding cognitive function, the patient states that he feels better and does not feel lost when talking to someone anymore. His daughter and sister-in-law agree with this assessment.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports urinary incontinence, adult hydrocephalus, gait impairment, and cognitive impairment.

MEDICATIONS AND ALLERGIES

Patient reports no medications or allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Constitutional: Rosenthalian appearance for impaired ability to carry out daily functions without evidence of unintentional weight loss.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain.
Neurological: Cranial nerves are equal with no disartria. EOMs are intact. Face symmetric. Motor strength is normal for bulk but coordination is slow from no finger to nose test.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
CT scan of the head from 10/15/2020 shows frontal horn span at the level of foramen of Munro of 4.6 cm, 3rd ventricular contour flat with span of 10 mm, substantial small vessel ischemic change.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Adult hydrocephalus, gait impairment, urinary incontinence and urgency, and cognitive impairment.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient underwent shunt placement on August 1st, 2020 for adult hydrocephalus with spino-catheter protocol in June 2020 due to progressive gait impairment, cognitive impairment, and decreased bladder control. He has been doing much better since his shunt surgery but still requires assistance with ambulation at times and wears diapers due to urinary incontinence.
• Patient Education and Counseling: The patient was counseled regarding his current status as well as the risks associated with driving after shunt placement.
• Medical Treatment: Continue follow-up in three months.

Amanda Taylor is a 72-year-old female who presents for a follow-up for hypertension. Her history includes significant alcohol use disorder and MI. After presenting at 150/100, she was prescribed hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg by mouth once daily, and lisinopril 20 mg by mouth once daily. CMP and CBC were essentially unremarkable.

The patient reports that she has been drinking alcohol 4 to 5 times a week to excess. She states that she has been drinking hard alcohol for a while and that she feels lethargic and tired when taking the full dose of lisinopril. She denies chest tightness or pressure or any shortness of breath.

The patient is taking her blood pressure medications as prescribed but only takes half of the lisinopril due to side effects. She denies any symptoms of medication side effects.

Patient reports history of hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, alcohol use disorder, and myocardial infarction (MI).

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports no tobacco use or substance abuse.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, or weight loss.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
• Neurological: Denies tremors or seizures.
• Psychiatric: Denies anxiety, agitation, or depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• General Examination: The patient is alert and pleasant in no acute distress. Skin is moist with good trigger. Head at 90 degrees. JVP flat.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for a follow-up for hypertension. Her history includes significant alcohol use disorder and MI. At her last visit on April 16th, her blood pressure was 130/90. • Additional Testing: Influenza vaccination recommended due to deferral status.

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Tyler Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. He last presented to the clinic on 03/04/2021, at which time he received a steroid injection in his right knee. He reports that the injection did not provide relief for more than 2 weeks. He states that his knee is still swollen and painful, and he has been experiencing pain at night when he gets up from sitting. He rates his pain level as 3 out of 10, but notes that it typically increases to a 6 on a normal day. The swelling began approximately 2 months ago, after he stopped wearing compression socks.

The patient reports that he has been taking his Xeljanz XR as directed and Celebrex 200 mg daily for the past 2 months. He states that the Celebrex has been helpful until the onset of swelling again.

The patient denies any improvement with compression socks and notes that they only provide some degree of relief.

He denies any improvement with compression socks and notes that they only provide some degree of relief.

The patient reports that he has been slowing down due to pain, but when he is sitting for a while, the pain becomes worse when he tries to get up. He states that this is very difficult and requires him to use a cane to get his bearings. However, after a short period of time, the pain loosens up.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he received a steroid injection in his right knee on 03/04/2021.
note.objective_exam:

MSK: Examination of the right knee reveals mild effusion with decreased range of motion. There is pitting edema around the knee and ankle bilaterally. Capillary refill is normal in the toes.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was performed today in office due to swelling and pain in this area.

note.assessment_and_plan:

Osteoarthritis.

His last visit was on 03/04/2021 when he received a steroid injection in his right knee which did not provide relief for more than 2 weeks. He presents today with persistent swelling and pain in this area.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed alternative treatments such as dietary modifications including reducing salt intake, elevating his legs at night, using compression stockings, physical therapy, or surgery if necessary.
• Medical Treatment: We will proceed with fluid aspiration and steroid injection procedure today in office due to swelling and pain in this area. I explained the risks, benefits, and alternatives were discussed with him prior to proceeding with this procedure.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right upper quadrant pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right upper quadrant pain. The onset of his pain began several weeks ago. He describes the pain as severe and squeezing in nature, which is located on the right side of his abdomen, just below his ribs. He rates his pain an 8 out of 10. The patient states that he has noticed that his pain is worse after eating, but it also occurs a couple of hours after eating. He denies any weight loss or vomiting.

The patient reports that he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and has been managing with diet and exercise since then. He states that he has cut back on sugar and started a keto diet, which has resulted in weight loss over the last 3 months. His blood sugars have improved, but he still experiences right upper quadrant pain.

The patient reports that he enjoys nature photography and notes that he will have to cut out pork rinds from his diet due to their high fat content.

PAST HISTORY

Family History: The patient reports that both parents have had cholecystectomies.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient enjoys nature photography.

MEDICAL HISTORY

Medical: History of type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS REVIEWED IN PREVIOUS SECTION.
CONSTITUTIONAL: Denies fevers today.
NEURO: Regular rate and rhythm without ectopic beats, clicks, rubs or murmurs.
RESPIRATORY: Clear and equal bilaterally to auscultation.
CARDIOVASCULAR: Regular rate and rhythm without gallops, murmurs or rubs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Mild cholecystitis with gallstones.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's abdominal ultrasound shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. His symptoms began several weeks ago when he started eating more fatty foods after being diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. He denies any weight loss or vomiting but does report nausea when his symptoms are severe.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the risks associated with surgery as well as alternative treatment options such as dietary modifications alone or medical treatment for cholecystitis.
- Medical Treatment: Due to the severity of his symptoms despite dietary modifications, I am recommending surgical intervention for removal of the gallbladder via laparoscopic cholecystectomy today. We will discuss post-operative care in detail today including avoiding high fat foods post-operatively as well as increasing fiber intake to help prevent constipation post-operatively.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Right shoulder pain.

Matthew Allen is a pleasant 67-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right shoulder pain. He denies any numbness or tingling in his fingers, but does report that he is having difficulty lifting anything too heavy. He notes that he is right-handed and denies any previous orthopedic injuries to his right shoulder.

The patient reports that he has been taking Tylenol for pain, which has not provided any relief. His symptoms have not improved since the onset of his pain.

The patient reports that he is right-hand dominant.

The patient denies any current medications or allergies.
note.objective_exam:

Neck: No tenderness to palpation of the cervical spine. Full range of motion on head exam. No ecchymosis or bruising on the neck.
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of the posterior shoulder at the acromioclavicular joint. Decreased abduction and adduction to about 90 degrees only. Pain with supination and pronation of the right arm. Palpable radial radial artery pulse.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

- Additional Testing: CT scan of the right shoulder will be ordered.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

The patient reports that he is a non-smoker.

The patient reports taking metformin and Norvasc.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Shortness of Breath.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. Scott Miller is a 36-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began 3 days ago when he was playing soccer. He states that he felt a pop in his right knee and noticed swelling. The patient denies any history of trauma to the right knee.

The patient reports that his pain is between 6 and 7 out of 10. He notes that his pain has decreased with anti-inflammatory medication, but he is taking it regularly at this time. He states that he can bend his leg, but it hurts towards the end of the motion. He can straighten his leg, but it feels like he needs to help get it straightened. The patient is able to bear weight on his right knee, but it feels loose and does not feel normal.

The patient denies any constitutional symptoms such as fever, chills, or weight loss.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient works at a desk.
note.objective_exam:

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee injury.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's examination today was consistent with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear. His history and physical examination findings are suggestive of this diagnosis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with the patient the nature of his diagnosis and treatment options today. I advised him to limit his work activities due to pain and recommend wearing a knee immobilizer and using crutches when walking around.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an MRI to evaluate the integrity of the ACL today. In addition, we will start him on meloxicam 50 mg daily for anti-inflammatory effects. I advised him to ice if necessary if he continues to see swelling and pain.
- Additional Testing: MRI ordered today.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
