Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Teresa Sullivan is a pleasant 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of her pain began 4 days ago. She states that she has been doing pottery and baking, and she has been working on a ceramic bowl for her son's birthday. She denies any history of trauma to the elbow. The patient rates her pain level at 7/10 at its worst.

The patient reports that her pain radiates down her arm and along the inside of her arm. She denies any numbness or tingling in her arm or hand. The patient states that she has not had any previous injuries to the elbow.

The patient reports that she is taking ibuprofen, but it is not helping with her pain. She has tried ice, but it is not helping either. She denies any fever or chills.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension and diabetes type 2.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is a baker and enjoys baking cakes and cinnamon rolls. She states that she loves to bake and makes these treats for family gatherings.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking lisinopril 10 mg daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Normal respiratory rate, oxygen saturation 100% on room air, no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
• Cardiovascular: Equal pulses bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• X-ray of the right elbow: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right elbow pain.
- Medical Reasoning: This appears to be medial epicondylitis due to overuse and damage to the tendons in the right arm.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed alternative activities with the patient today, including holding off on pottery for a couple of weeks to allow for healing time.
- Medical Treatment: We will start a sling for the right arm today. I am going to order ice packs for 20 minutes three times a day. I am going to prescribe 600 mg ibuprofen three times a day with food for one week. We will follow up in two weeks if there is no improvement in symptoms.
- Additional Testing: X-ray was performed today which shows no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality supporting our medical diagnosis today.
2. Diabetes type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood sugar levels have been elevated at times when she eats sweets, which may be contributing to her elevated blood sugar levels at times when she eats sweets.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with the patient today including limiting sweets and increasing protein intake when eating sweets.
- Medical Treatment: We are going to increase metformin from 500 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily starting immediately today. I am going to order an A1C test as well as refer her out for diabetic counseling at this point in time as well as follow up with me in two weeks regarding her diabetes status.
3. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: Her blood pressure has been stable on lisinopril at this point in time which may be due to increased physical activity.

Right knee pain.

The patient is a 68-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. He states that he injured his right knee 2.5 weeks ago when he stepped off a curb. He denies any actual fall but states that he turned his ankle to the outside and thought that was going to hurt the most, but after the ankle soreness resolved, he noticed that his knee hurt and it clicks when he walks. The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen for pain, but it does not impact his pain during the day as he works through it. He denies any pain at rest or when sitting with his foot flat on the floor. The patient is able to perform a full squat without pain, but this is when he feels the most clicking. He denies any numbness or tingling in his foot at all.

The patient reports that he has fractured his 2nd toe 3 times over the last 10 years and currently has numbness in his right foot depending on what shoe he wears.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient works in sales and rides a bike for exercise.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking ibuprofen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain, left foot numbness.

Right heel pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right heel pain. The onset of his symptoms began 10 days ago. He reports that the pain is located in the posterior aspect of his heel and radiates proximally into his calf. The pain is aggravated by working out and when he first gets up in the morning. He runs 10 kilometers in the morning, bikes for 45 minutes to an hour at lunchtime, and swims for 30 minutes to an hour in the evening. He trains 5 days per week and alternates between a long run and a long bike ride on weekends. He does not stretch at all.

The patient reports that his symptoms are worse after activity, but also present when he first wakes up in the morning. He describes his pain as tight and almost like it is tearing. It eases up after he has been walking around for about 10-15 minutes, but if he sits down for any extended period of time and then tries to get back up, it is sore again.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he is currently training for a triathlon.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the lower extremities reveals no left leg pain. The right leg is tender over the plantar fascia bilaterally but more so on the right side. There is tenderness over the Achilles tendon bilaterally but more so on the right side with palpation of both sides of the tendon bilaterally there is no pain with palpation of both calf muscles bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right heel pain.

Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with Achilles tendinitis due to overuse.
Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed with him that this will require some time off from training before we move into next phase.

Referral: I have referred him to physical therapy for strength and stretching education as well as treatment.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christina Cooper is a pleasant 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that she has had this ulcer for approximately 1 year. She states that it started as a small blister and then she picked at it, which became red and infected. She was treated with antibiotics, which seemed to improve her symptoms, but they have not resolved. The patient denies any pain but states that she does not have much sensation in her foot. She reports increased drainage and fatigue.

The patient has type 2 diabetes and her last hemoglobin A1c was 10. She is currently taking insulin and metformin.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports no pain in the right foot but denies sensation.
Skin: Reports increased drainage from the ulcer.
Neurological: Reports decreased sensation in the right foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right foot reveals a 1.2 cm x 2 cm circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, proximal to the 5th MTP joint. There is yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. No surrounding erythema or cellulitis is present. There is no evidence of fluid collection or necrosis. No odor is appreciated, and there is no bony exposure when palpated over the wound site. The patient denies pain when touching the wound site.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was performed prior to today's visit and revealed no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient has a diabetic foot ulcer.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's diabetes likely contributed to her current presentation as she has type 2 diabetes and neuropathy.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with regards to her diabetes management today.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an ankle brachial index (ABI) today to assess for adequate blood flow to her lower extremities. Debridement will be performed in office today to remove dead tissue from her wound site. I have prescribed colaganase ointment for use once daily on top of dressing changes until we see improvement in size of her wound.
- Additional Testing: An ABI will be ordered today.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up after STEMI.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Anderson is a pleasant 74-year-old female who presents for follow-up after an interior STEMI where we had to put in another stent. She was doing well after her last heart attack, but she started having this horrible chest pain that wouldn’t go away. She went to the emergency room and was told she needed another stent. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath.

The patient has been walking her dog every day for the past 6 months and states that she is doing fine. She denies any exercise at all since her last visit. The patient has noticed that her legs are a little swollen since they sent her home from the hospital.

The patient reports that she is able to lie flat at night when she sleeps. She uses 2 pillows and sometimes sits up a bit more but thinks it’s pretty normal. The patient states that she is able to afford her medications and is taking them as prescribed.

Regarding diet, the patient admits that she has not adjusted her salt intake since her last heart attack but will have to go back to watching the salt intake. Her favorite foods are pizza and Tries, which are probably her second favorite food. The patient enjoys pepperoni on pizza occasionally with vegetables, but acknowledges that pepperoni is high in salt on top of a cheesy pizza.

The patient reports that she has been watching her sugars because she does not want to go on insulin and is taking metformin as prescribed. She walks her dog because she is trying to stay active.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient walks her dog daily and enjoys pizza and tries (a type of food).

MEDICATIONS

Aspirin 81 mg daily; Brilinta 90 mg twice daily; Lipitor 80 mg daily; Toprol 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; metformin.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: No carotid bruits.
Heart: S3 gallop at LBE, grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at LBE.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Extremities: Lower extremity edema, pitting edema grade +1 on right radial artery.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
EKG: Normal sinus rhythm, good R wave progression, evolutionary changes anticipated after STEMI.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents for follow-up after an interior STEMI where we had to put in another stent. She was doing well after her last heart attack, but she started having this horrible chest pain that wouldn’t go away. We reviewed the EKG results today which show normal sinus rhythm with good R wave progression and evolutionary changes anticipated after STEMI.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Concerns about medications.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jose Thompson is a 75-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for a routine checkup. He was last seen 3 months ago. The patient reports that he is doing okay, but he is concerned about all the medications he is taking. He states that he has been taking his aspirin and Brilinta as prescribed, but he has been taking fish oil as well. He denies any side effects from the medications.

The patient had a heart attack 6 months ago and underwent stent placement at the left anterior descending artery. He was placed on aspirin and Brilinta for long-term use to prevent further cardiac events. His most recent hemoglobin A1c was 16, which is elevated. He reports that his glucose levels are approximately 130 fasting.

The patient has diabetes and lives with his dog, San Francisco 49ers fan.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Heart attack, coronary artery disease, diabetes.
Surgical: Stent placement at the left anterior descending artery.
SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives with his dog.
Social: Lives in San Francisco.
MEDICATIONS

Aspirin; Brilinta; Fish oil; Crestor; Metoprolol 50 mg once a day.
ALLERGIES

Contrast dye.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits appreciated.
• Heart: Slight grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
• Lower extremities: One plus nonpitting edema.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Kidney function stable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient had a heart attack 6 months ago and underwent stent placement at the left anterior descending artery. He was placed on aspirin and Brilinta for long-term use to prevent further cardiac events. His most recent hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 16, which is consistent with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus contributing to his coronary artery disease. The patient denies any side effects from his medications.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with the patient that he will need to continue on aspirin and Brilinta for long-term use to prevent further cardiac events. I also discussed with him that managing his diabetes will play an important role in his coronary artery disease management. I referred him for cardiac rehab so that he can be more active and have confidence in exercising again.
- Medical Treatment: Refill prescription for metoprolol 50 mg once daily as well as Crestor 40 mg once daily as well as aspirin indefinitely due to stent placement at LAD artery.
- Additional Testing: No additional testing needed at this time but if symptoms develop again we will proceed with further testing such as stress test if necessary.
• Stage III chronic kidney disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient has stage III chronic kidney disease based on his creatinine level which indicates stable kidney function despite having contrast dye recently administered due to prior history of kidney issues from contrast dye exposure in the past. The patient denies taking Motrin or Advil due to concerns of renal toxicity from these medications but states he has stopped taking them altogether due to this concern.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with the patient that it is very important for him to follow up with his nephrologist regularly so that we can monitor his kidney function closely going forward. I also advised him not to take Motrin or Advil anymore due to concerns of renal toxicity from these medications but encouraged him not to stop taking them altogether without consulting me first if they are needed for pain control due to potential risks of renal toxicity from these medications if taken without medical supervision in this case however we have alternative options available such as Tylenol which should be safe for him to take if needed for pain control going forward.
- Medical Treatment: Referral made for appointment with Dr Miller, Nephrologist, today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Barbara White is a 31-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of abdominal pain. The onset of her pain began 1 week ago. She reports that she has been drinking a lot of coffee lately and believes that this may have triggered her gastritis. She denies fever with her pain. The patient states that her abdominal pain is located on both sides of her upper abdomen and increases with exercise. She reports nausea and vomiting on and off, which she estimates has occurred 3 times in the past week.

The patient notes that she has been drinking more coffee and believes this may be related to her abdominal pain. She states that she started drinking more coffee last week and her coffee intake was pretty bad towards the end of last week, but she has been controlling herself this week and estimates that she probably only had 1 cup this week.

The patient denies any recent asthma attacks, but notes that she sometimes forgets to take her Flovent twice daily. She states that she will continue taking the Flovent daily and will use albuterol as needed for wheezing.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of diabetes type 2, asthma, gastritis, and moderately heavy alcohol use.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is a smoker.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior exam.
Respiratory: Mild end expiratory wheezes very faint otherwise normal lung exam with excellent air movement.
Gastrointestinal: Mild tenderness in the epigastrium of the abdomen. Abdomen is otherwise soft. No tenderness in the right lower quadrant or right upper quadrant.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute gastritis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with acute gastritis. Her history of diabetes type 2, asthma, and moderately heavy alcohol use are also present but do not seem to be contributing factors at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to cut back on alcohol consumption to less than 2-3 drinks per week as well as reduce caffeine intake as these may be contributing factors to her gastritis.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Zantac for symptom relief.
- Additional Testing: Urinalysis, urine pregnancy test, CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel will be ordered for further evaluation.
2. Diabetes Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood glucose level was under control at last visit when we increased metformin from 500 mg once daily to 500 mg twice daily which seems to be effective in controlling blood glucose levels at present time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient to continue checking her blood glucose levels when she comes back in for follow up in 4 weeks.
- Medical Treatment: We will continue metformin 1000 mg once daily in the morning and 500 mg once daily in the evening at this point we will see how it goes over time if needed we can always increase or decrease medication dosage at that point.
3. Asthma.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's asthma symptoms have been well controlled on Flovent twice daily with albuterol as needed for wheezing at this point we will continue Flovent twice daily as well as albuterol as needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 6 months ago, but they have been more persistent over the last month. She reports that she experiences pain with typing on the keyboard, but not with mouse use. She has been taking ibuprofen for pain relief, which seems to help. The patient denies nocturnal pain or sleep disturbance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right hand numbness and tingling.
Neurological: Reports right hand numbness and tingling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right hand reveals decreased grip strength bilaterally. Pain on extension and flexion of the wrist. Positive Tinel's sign.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Outpatient EMG/NCV ordered.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right carpal tunnel syndrome.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome. She works on a keyboard all day, which is a common cause of this condition.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed conservative treatment options including wrist splinting, physical therapy, and medication management.
- Medical Treatment: We will start her in a wrist splint at night to help alleviate her symptoms. I have also recommended that she increase her ibuprofen to 600 mg 4 times daily for pain management. We will order an outpatient EMG/NCV to confirm the diagnosis.
- Additional Testing: Outpatient EMG/NCV ordered.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a pleasant 59-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. He states that he hurt his elbow about a week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He denies any history of trauma to the area. The onset of pain was sudden and he describes it as sharp in nature. He notes that the pain is located at the tip of his elbow and radiates down to his forearm. He denies any radiation of pain to his arm or hand. The patient reports that he has been taking Advil for 2 days, which has helped somewhat with his pain.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a past medical history of hypertension and diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he plays lacrosse with his children.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is currently taking Lisinopril 20 mg daily and Metformin 500 mg daily.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Right elbow contusion.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury to his right elbow when he was hit by a lacrosse stick while playing with his children. This resulted in swelling, inflammation, and bruising at the olecranon area of the posterior elbow. His x-ray was unremarkable for any bony abnormalities.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him to avoid playing lacrosse with his son for the next couple of weeks to allow time for healing.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed him 800 mg ibuprofen twice daily for pain management and ice therapy 3 times a day for 20 minutes at a time to help reduce swelling and pain.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood pressure was elevated at today's visit, but this appears to be white coat hypertension as he denies any symptoms or changes in diet or medication use.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him that he is doing well on diet and medication, but we will continue to monitor blood pressure closely in clinic today.
- Medical Treatment: We will continue him on Lisinopril 20 mg daily as prescribed.
3. Diabetes Mellitus Type 2.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood sugar levels have been stable since initiating Metformin therapy, but we will obtain an A1C level today to confirm this stability and assess if further adjustments are needed in medication dosage.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acute on chronic congestive heart failure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kevin Davis is an 82-year-old male with a past medical history significant for hypertension and stage 3 chronic kidney disease. He presents for hospital follow-up after an acute on chronic congestive heart failure exacerbation. The patient reports that he has been trying to watch his diet as recommended by the physician, but he noticed that his ankles were swelling. He also states that he was trying to watch his diet, but he really noticed that his ankles were swelling and then one day he got really super short of breath and he even had to call 911. The paramedics put him on the special mask to breathe when he got to the ER, the doctor in the ER said his blood pressure was super high.

The patient denies chest pain since he has been home.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Hypertension, Stage 3 chronic kidney disease.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports being a football fan.

MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking Bumex 2 mg once daily, Cozaar 100 mg daily, and Norvasc 5 mg once daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur stable. Lungs are clear bilaterally. No wheezes or rales heard. Bilateral lower extremities show trace edema.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Echocardiogram shows preserved ejection fraction of 55% abnormal diastolic filling and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute on chronic congestive heart failure.
- Medical Reasoning: This was caused by dietary indiscretion in uncontrolled hypertension.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed dietary modifications with the patient today. I advised him to continue taking Bumex 2 mg once daily and avoid salty foods such as pizza and chicken wings. I also advised him to weigh himself every day and call me if he gains more than 3 pounds in two days.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Bumex 2 mg once daily.
- Additional Testing: Continue monitoring for any signs of worsening heart failure.
2. Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is currently compliant with medication but has not been consistent with medication adherence due to missing doses at times.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed dietary modifications with the patient today. I advised him to continue taking Cozaar 100 mg daily and Norvasc 5 mg once daily. I also advised him to follow up with a nutritionist for further education on healthy eating options.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Cozaar 100 mg daily and Norvasc 5 mg once daily. Order renal artery ultrasound due to uncontrolled hypertension at this time.
3. Stage 3 chronic kidney disease.
- Medical Reasoning: We need more labs done at this time due to uncontrolled hypertension at this time.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain and swelling after a fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain and swelling after a fall. The onset of symptoms began yesterday when he was taking out the trash and slipped on ice. He was being very careful, but he noticed that there was a small patch of ice. He was on the ground and was being very careful. He initially could not bear weight on his right ankle, but he was able to ambulate with assistance. He kept his right ankle elevated, iced it, and took ibuprofen for pain relief. His symptoms have improved slightly today.

The patient has been playing soccer for the community league for many years. He has had several injuries in the past, but he cannot recall if he ever injured his right ankle.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he enjoys playing soccer for the community league.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he enjoys playing soccer for the community league.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he takes ibuprofen as needed for pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and swelling.

Neurological Examination: Capillary refill is less than 3 seconds with strong dorsalis pedis pulse. Sensation is intact to light touch in all extremities.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right ankle sprain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with a right ankle sprain given his history of playing soccer and his current presentation.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I reviewed the nature of his condition with him today and advised him to keep his leg elevated when seated, continue icing, use an Aircast to stabilize the ankle, use crutches for 1-2 days, then ambulate as tolerated.
- Medical Treatment: Continue NSAIDs as needed for pain relief.
- Additional Testing: Review of x-ray results pending.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated cholesterol.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Cruz is a 17-year-old non-binary imminesipated minor who presents for evaluation of newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia. The patient is here at the clinic today because she was told that her cholesterol level was elevated at her annual checkup and she wishes to have this evaluated further. The patient reports that she has been riding her bike on trails and enjoys being outside. She states that she tries to eat a clean diet most days, but admits to consuming chocolate chip cookies. She denies any history of hypercholesterolemia or anemia at an early age, but notes that her grandparents had their cholesterol checked last year and were told it was borderline. The patient reports that they were advised to watch their diet, but they are unsure what is going on with their cholesterol levels now.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that her parents smoked when they lived with them.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient enjoys being outside and riding her bike on trails. She states that she keeps pretty active during the week.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies fatigue, weight loss, or weight gain.
Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or nausea.
Psychiatric: Reports no issues with growing up or feeling like a girl.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS IN REVIEWED AND LOOK GOOD TODAY.
NECK EXAM: No thyroid goiter present.
EYES: Extraocular movements are normal in all directions. No Zonthomas present.
NECK EXAM: No thyroid goiter present.
RESPIRATORY: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
Cholesterol level elevated at 210.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Elevated Cholesterol Level.
- Medical Reasoning: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends screening for elevated cholesterol levels in children between the ages of 9-11 and again between 17-20 years of age. Studies have shown a link between high cholesterol and premature heart attacks. We will order a full cholesterol panel, glucose, complete metabolic panel, thyroid studies, liver panels, and genetic testing to determine if this problem is familial or secondary in nature.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including dietary changes with the patient today. I encouraged her to follow up with a nutritionist for further guidance on healthy eating habits. I also encouraged her to continue biking as it is a great form of exercise for cardiovascular health.
- Medical Treatment: We will follow up in 3-6 months after the patient has met with the nutritionist and has instituted dietary changes for repeat cholesterol level testing.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sophia Jackson is a pleasant 30-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 6 months ago. She denies any specific event that caused the pain. The patient describes her pain as a deep achy pain located behind her patella. She states that she can hear creaking in her knees when she moves. Her pain is exacerbated by ambulation from a seated position, as well as stair climbing and watching TV. The patient notes that rest typically helps with her pain.

The patient reports that she has tried ice and an ACE bandage in the past, but she tries to avoid taking any medications due to side effects. She denies any swelling or redness in her knees.

The patient is an avid runner and has been running 5-6 miles per day, but she has had to decrease her mileage significantly due to knee pain. She runs on a treadmill during the winter months, but prefers running outdoors.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she sustained an upper extremity fracture when she was in 6th grade.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she works from home and is active, enjoying running 5-6 miles per day.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking ibuprofen and Aleve as needed.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS REVIEWED IN OFFICE TODAY ARE WITHIN NORMAL LIMITS.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the lower extremities reveals normal gait. Strength is 3/5 for abduction of legs bilaterally, with 5/5 strength for the remainder of lower extremities. There is tenderness to palpation over the bilateral retinacula and positive patellar grind test bilaterally. Lachman anterior and posterior drawer and McMurray tests are negative bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of bilateral knees were obtained today and reviewed in office today, which show no fractures or osteoarthritis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with patellofemoral pain syndrome based on her history, physical examination, and radiographic findings today.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the nature of this condition with the patient today, including its common etiology in active young individuals, as well as treatment options available to her at this time.
• Medical Treatment: I recommended that she continue taking ibuprofen or anti-inflammatory medication as needed for symptom management at home today.
• Additional Testing: X-rays were obtained today which showed no fractures or osteoarthritis.
• Additional Therapy: I recommended that she begin physical therapy to address any incorrect running mechanics and increase lower extremity strength and mobility.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Lumbar back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kyle Morales is a pleasant 58-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of lumbar back pain. The onset of his pain began 2 weeks ago when he was lifting a box of books. He denies any history of trauma. He describes his pain as achy and sharp, initially localized to his low back but now radiating down his left leg. He denies any numbness, tingling, or weakness. He states that he is able to sit without any discomfort.

The patient reports that he has tried taking ibuprofen and Tylenol, which sometimes helps with his pain.

The patient denies any loss of bladder or bowel control.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that his father has back pain.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he is an Olympic weightlifter and plays soccer in the midfield position. He denies smoking.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports back pain. Denies left leg pain, numbness, tingling, weakness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg; Respiratory rate 18.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the musculoskeletal system reveals midline tenderness at the L4-L5 disk space with right-sided lumbar paravertebral tenderness. Pain with lumbar flexion. Supine straight leg test is positive.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the lumbar spine revealed disc desiccation and a disc bulge with paracentral disc herniation resulting in moderate right neuroforaminal stenosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lumbar back pain due to a herniated disk with radiculopathy.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with a herniated disk with nerve impingement at the L4-L5 level.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed the nature of his condition, treatment options, and risks associated with spinal injections in detail today. I provided him with paperwork for review prior to his procedure today.
• Medical Treatment: We will proceed with a spinal injection under fluoroscopy today. This will include an injection of a strong NSAID and corticosteroid into the lumbar spine to help reduce inflammation causing his pain.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela Powell is an 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left knee pain. The onset of her pain began 1 week ago when she was running with her 5-year-old niece. She states that she twisted her knee in a funky way and heard a pop. She rates her pain as a 4 out of 10 initially but notes that it has increased to a throbbing type of pain. The patient denies hearing a pop when she was running with her niece, however, she does report that she twisted her knee.

The patient reports that she has been limping since the onset of her pain and has not had any improvement. She states that she is able to bear weight on the left leg but notes that it hurts more on the medial aspect than the lateral aspect. The patient denies any improvement with ibuprofen due to an allergy to ibuprofen and notes that Tylenol helps some but only for short periods of time before the pain returns.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she runs with her niece.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of ulcer.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left knee pain, limping, swelling, effusion, and decreased range of motion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Left Knee Examination: Examination reveals edema and effusion in the left knee. There is moderate range of motion bilaterally but not fully. Pain on flexion and extension bilaterally. Negative Lachman's test and negative valgus and varus test.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of the left knee were obtained today and reviewed in office today. These are unremarkable for any fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Left knee strain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained an injury when running with her niece which resulted in medial collateral ligament strain.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed treatment options with the patient today including ice, compression, elevation, and immobilization as well as oral medication for pain management.
• Medical Treatment: I have prescribed tramadol 50 mg twice daily for pain management. I have also recommended ice 3-4 times per day for 20-30 minutes at a time as well as compression bandage use for immobilization. The patient will wear a knee immobilizer for the next week to keep the knee from moving so it can heal a little bit and reduce some inflammation that is present here at this time.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

High blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diane Baker is a 28-year-old female with a past medical history significant for depression and hypertension who presents for emergency room follow-up. The patient reports that she has been experiencing elevated blood pressure, which has been occurring once a week, sometimes reaching up to 200. She states that she has been traveling a lot for work and is not eating well during these times. She denies taking her blood pressure cuff with her while traveling. The patient reports that she is taking lisinopril as prescribed.

The patient states that she was seen in the emergency room yesterday because she was feeling lightheaded and started to fall. She was caught by her boyfriend and they went to the emergency room. Her blood pressure was elevated at the time of presentation, but it has since been controlled.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing headaches.

The patient reports that she started therapy last year and has been going once a week. She states that this has helped her with her depression.

The patient reports that her support system is great, including her boyfriend, mom, and brother.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fatigue, weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain, shortness of breath.
• Respiratory: Reports nasal congestion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No carotid bruits present in the neck.
Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at auscultation of the heart. No murmurs or gallops heard at auscultation of the lungs bilaterally. Trace pitting edema to the lower extremities bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Electrocardiogram stable in comparison to last year.
Echocardiogram from just a few months ago shows slightly leaky heart valve with no treatment options available at this time. The heart murmur is stable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. High Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure remains elevated despite current medication and lifestyle modifications. We will increase lisinopril to 40 mg once daily and have the patient continue to check her blood pressures through the patient portal and report them back to me for further evaluation if necessary or if we need to add a second agent.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications with the patient today including regular exercise, healthy eating, stress reduction techniques, and adequate sleep per night.
- Medical Treatment: Lisinopril increased to 40 mg once daily.
2. Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient denies any current symptoms of depression but does report that therapy has helped her in the past when she was last seen in clinic last year. We will continue monitoring her symptoms without initiating new medication at this time but will contact me if needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up to abnormal lab findings.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joyce Price is a 50-year-old female with a past medical history significant for COPD, congestive heart failure who presents for follow-up to an abnormal lab finding. The patient reports she has been feeling tired lately. She states that over the past couple of months, she has noticed that her energy has really gone down. She used to be really active, just trying to be as healthy as she can be, running, climbing. She at least tries to do an hour or two a day. And over the past month, it has gone slowly downhill. She states she has not been able to keep up with the way she was going with her exercise.

The patient denies any blood in her stools at this time. She also denies spotting with her periods.

The patient endorses fatigue and dizziness but denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, body aches.

She reports noticing a little bit of weight loss but attributes this to doing well with her exercise.

Regarding her COPD, the patient reports that it has been okay. She states that after quitting smoking several years ago, she quit cold turkey and has not gone back since. She believes that during the changes of season it gets a little bit harder for her to breathe but thinks this is just due to allergies.

From a congestive heart failure standpoint, the patient reports watching her diet and salt intake. She states she has been staying away from French fries and other salty foods that she loves to eat and everything looks great.

The patient denies swelling in her legs or any other extremity edema.

She feels like she has a good support system as she mentions having a boyfriend and brother nearby.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Clear bilaterally without wheezes or rales. Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at auscultation of the heart exam.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Labs are within normal limits; Anemia labs are still pending.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Anemia: The patient's hemoglobin level is 8.2 which is below normal for someone of this age group (13-14). We need to investigate why it is low.
- Endoscopy and colonoscopy ordered due to suspicion of gastrointestinal bleeding.
- Follow up in 1 week for further workup once labs return.
2. COPD: The patient's COPD appears stable at this time but we will continue monitoring her closely as needed.
- Continue avoiding smoking.
3. Congestive heart failure: The patient's congestive heart failure appears stable at this time but we will continue monitoring her closely as needed.
- Continue Toprol XL; Lisinopril 20 mg daily; Lasix 20 mg daily.

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Evelyn Morris is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease, prior carpal tunnel release, and a herniated disc who presents for her annual exam. She has been doing okay over the last year. Her back has been doing well. She has not had any back pain or any limitations in movement, so that is doing well. She had steroid injections for her back a couple of months ago, and that is doing well.

She had carpal tunnel issues that were fixed a couple of years ago. She is back to work and has not had any issues. She has full range of motion and it feels really good. She denies any numbness or tingling in her hands.

She has prior stenting in the past for her heart and her heart vessels. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea or vomiting over the last month. The chest pain happens when she walks but it does go away if she rests. It does not occur at rest.

She describes the chest pain as feeling like a burn. It is located in the middle of her chest right here. She endorses this chest pressure 3 times per week.

She denies lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever chills.

The patient reports she has had some nasal congestion due to allergies because of pollen.
note.objective_exam:

• Cardiovascular: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at auscultation over LLS; no carotid bruits; no lower extremity edema.

note.assessment_and_plan:

1) Carpal Tunnel Release: No further treatment needed at this time as she seems to be doing well with full range of motion and no symptoms.
2) Herniated Disc: No further steroid injections or physical therapy needed at this time as she seems to be doing well with no symptoms.
3) Coronary Artery Disease: Continue aspirin and Toprol XL as prescribed.
- Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages causing chest discomfort.
- Lipid panel ordered and statinitis started at 20 mg once daily.

She reports that she had routine blood work done last week and they said that her blood sugars were high, so she should come in and talk to me and get some more work done and see why that is.

The patient denies any symptoms. She was a little shocked when she came back high and elevated, so hopefully we can figure out what's going on.

She has been on metformin 1000 mg daily. She increased her dose last time. The patient confirms that she is currently taking.

The patient denies any urinary symptoms such as difficulty urinating or burning when urinating.

She reports that her diet has been great lately. She has been avoiding sugars, watching her weight, and power walking every day. She was a little surprised when the blood work came back elevated.

The patient checks her blood sugars in the morning and fasting blood sugars.

She reports that her high blood pressure has been good and stable. She is stable on lisinopril for this condition. The patient uses a home cuff to monitor her BP at home, which has been normal.

The patient had an ACL repair on her right knee about 5 years ago. Everything is going well so far. She has not had any issues with mobility. The patient is pretty physically active with power walking about 30 minutes every day.

• Constitutional: Denies headaches or belly pain today except for the abnormal blood work.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Followup of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Bruce Howard is a 60-year-old male with a past medical history, significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension. He presents for followup of his chronic problems.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression. He states that he has been going for long walks outside every morning over the summer. He enjoyed this activity and it encouraged him to do some yard work on the weekends. However, he has not been able to continue this due to the cold weather and is looking for alternative options. The patient denies any thoughts of harming himself or others.

Regarding his diabetes, the patient reports that he got through Halloween okay but did not stick to his diet too much during the Thanksgiving week. He states that he has been trying to monitor his blood sugar levels more closely.

The patient reports that he is still taking metformin and lisinopril as prescribed. He denies any issues with these medications.

The patient reports that he purchased a blood pressure cuff as recommended by the physician and has been using it regularly. His blood pressure appears to be well controlled at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath on exertion.
• Neurological: Denies blood in stool or hematochezia.
• Psychiatric: Denies suicidal ideation.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Maria Martin is a pleasant 75-year-old female who presents for a follow-up visit. She has been informed and consents to have this visit recorded.

The patient reports that she has been doing well, but her blood sugars are not well controlled. She received a letter from the clinic last time she was seen, and she has been taking the 2 mg glimepiride twice daily. The patient denies increasing her glimepiride dosage.

The patient reports that she is trying to eat healthier, but she does not like pasta and only eats wheat bread when available. She states that she drinks club soda and seltzer water instead of regular water. She denies drinking any sodas.

The patient reports that her eye exams are up-to-date, but she sees a different optometrist each time due to changes in doctors at Liberty Road.

She reports that her blood pressure was 116/0 mmHg two weeks ago. The patient is on a combination of medications for hypertension, including metoprolol 50 mg once daily, lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/25 mg once daily, and amlodipine 10 mg once daily. The patient denies taking all of these medications as prescribed.

The patient reports that she is tolerating atorvastatin well but states that her feet feel like hell due to peripheral neuropathy. She also experiences pain up to her hip.

The patient denies headaches or dizziness. Her vision with cataract surgery is good except for one lens which is not happy with it. She had iodine for her eyes and then waited a month before getting healed up before the doctor wrote the prescription.

She reports coughing lately due to congestion. The coughing appears clear when it comes up. The patient denies fever, chills, shortness of breath, chest pain or pressure or tightness, nausea, vomiting or GI symptoms.

Her urinary symptoms include slower stream but stable urination several times per day with occasional nighttime urination after drinking in the evening.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No constitutional complaints such as fevers or chills.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
• Medical Reasoning: Her A1c was elevated at 9.9% last time we saw her in clinic; we want to increase the glimepiride dosage from 2 mg twice daily to 4 mg twice daily as recommended by our clinic letter last time we saw her in clinic today.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed dietary modifications with the patient today including reducing carbohydrate intake and increasing fiber intake as well as staying hydrated with water instead of soda or other sugary drinks.
• Medical Treatment: Continue metformin as prescribed; increase glimepiride dosage from 2 mg twice daily to 4 mg twice daily; continue lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide; continue atorvastatin; continue metoprolol; continue amlodipine; quit smoking.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluating right hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Mr. Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old right-handed male who presents today for the evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling. The onset of his symptoms began 2 weeks ago, after he noticed that his symptoms were worse than they were at the time of his motor vehicle accident in December 2019. He sustained a broken wrist at the time of the accident, which healed without surgery. He notes that he has been wearing a splint on both wrists since then, but his symptoms have worsened over the last month. He states that he wears the left wrist splint more frequently than the right, but his right wrist is worse. He denies any pain with palpation of his wrists or elbows.

The patient reports that he experiences numbness and tingling in both hands, which radiates from the middle and ring fingers on the right side to the pinky and ring fingers on the left side. His symptoms are worse at night and come and go throughout the day. He states that he feels soreness in his hands, which sometimes throb, but overall feels weaker when using them. The patient notes that when his symptoms are present, he experiences more tingling than pain.

The patient denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers. He also denies any weakness in his hands or fingers.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension for which he is taking Coreg. He also reports a history of anxiety for which he is taking Lexapro.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he has prediabetes, which was controlled via dietary changes.
He also reports a history of motor vehicle accident in December 2019 resulting in broken wrists; history of neck contusion from the accident; history of gout and muscle pain; history of floaters in eyes; history of dry, itchy skin and nail bed changes; history of easily fatigued and weight gain; history of excessive hunger and abdominal bloating; history of bilateral peripheral edema and shortness of breath.
He denies any known allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurological Examination: Examination reveals decreased sensation to pinprick over third and fourth digits on both hands bilaterally. Reflexes are 1+ bilaterally symmetric with downgoing toes bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.
1) Schedule EMG testing to determine exact location of nerve irritation.
2) If EMG testing confirms bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or cubital tunnel syndrome after completion, refer to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery or orthopedic referral for same treatment if necessary.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Kimberly Taylor is a 60-year-old right-handed female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral hand numbness and tingling. The onset of her symptoms began 2 weeks ago, after she sustained a motor vehicle accident in December of last year, in which she broke both wrists. She was treated with a splint for her right wrist, but has been wearing it on both wrists as well. She states that her symptoms have worsened over the last month.

The patient reports that she experiences numbness and tingling in both hands, particularly from her middle and ring fingers all the way up to her forearm on the right side, and more so on the left side with pain in her pinky and ring fingers. She describes her pain as sore, with throbbing at times. She states that she feels weaker when using her hands, especially at night when the pain goes away and then the tingling is just dull.

The patient denies any loss of sensation in her hands or fingers. She states that they are less sensitive than they should be, but she can still feel them. She was prescribed nerve pain medication which she has not been taking as directed.

Ms. Taylor reports that she has been experiencing mild stiffness in her neck as well, due to a contusion from hitting her head during the accident.

PAST HISTORY

Medical History: Chronic kidney disease; Prediabetes (diet controlled); Hypertension; Anxiety; GERD; Diabetes; Gout; History of MVA with broken wrists; Contusion from hitting head during MVA.

Current Medications: Carvedilol 25 mg twice daily; Lexapro 10 mg daily.
Allergies: Sulfa (causes rash).

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue and weight gain.
GI: Excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Floaters.
Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Positive diabetes, always hungry.
Skin: Nail bed trenches, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Gout, muscle pain.
Neurological: Parasthesia, bilateral hands.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
• Sensations normal except pin prick sensation diminished in the third and fourth fingers on the right side and fourth and fifth fingers on the left side. \\npinprick sensation diminished bilaterally.

RESULTS
No metastatic disease or acute intracranial abnormalities were seen on CT brain with and without contrast performed 02/05/21.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michelle King is a 35-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of acid reflux.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's history and physical examination reveal a several-year history of GERD with poorly controlled symptoms despite omeprazole therapy. Her symptoms are exacerbated by spicy foods, carbonated beverages, citrus products, and tomato-based products. Stress is also a trigger for her symptoms.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I have discussed the nature of her condition with the patient in detail today. I have advised her to avoid trigger foods and to work on stress management techniques such as deep breathing exercises or yoga.
• Medical Treatment: We will attempt dietary modifications first. If these do not improve her symptoms we will consider switching her to Nexium 40 mg twice daily. If these measures do not improve her symptoms we will consider a trial of protonix and obtain a pH-impedance study to rule out abnormal acid reflux exposure and determine if there is a functional etiology or hypersensitivity.
• Additional Testing: We will schedule an EGD for today at checkout desk.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acute to chronic constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 39-year-old female with a history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. She was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021, and was discharged on 07/02/2021. The patient is currently being followed up for concerns for spasms and lightheadedness, significant constipation, and reported diaphoresis. She was evaluated in the emergency department where she was febrile and had significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for ongoing urinary tract infection, but she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. In the end, she slowly improved. She does have a supra-pubic catheter.

Cultures were obtained and reviewed.

She presents today to follow up regarding these concerns.

The patient states that she believes her hospitalization was more likely due to her dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. She did have a lot of vital signs changes including blood pressure fluctuations. The patient feels like she has a good bowel regimen including taking MiraLAX regularly as a primary treatment for constipation issues as well as lactulose for severe constipation. She feels like this was less likely a true urinary tract infection and was just related to her constipation however we did have a good discussion regarding her leukocytosis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
• Respiratory: Denies cough or dyspnea.
• Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports constipation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Examination of the nervous system is unremarkable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Suprapubic catheter in place.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Acute to chronic constipation.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient believes that her hospitalization was more likely due to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. However, she does have a good bowel regimen including taking MiraLAX regularly as a primary treatment for constipation issues as well as lactulose for severe constipation. We discussed the possibility of an inflammatory bowel disease but we did not find any evidence of this on urinalysis.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the possibility of an inflammatory bowel disease but we did not find any evidence of this on urinalysis. I advised the patient that it would be beneficial to follow up in 3 weeks for updated fasting labs and CBCs to monitor her white blood cell count.
Quadriplegia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient has been doing well at home with regards to managing her dysreflexia symptoms however she does report experiencing lightheadedness at times which may be related to autonomic dysreflexia.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient that it would be beneficial to follow up in 3 weeks for updated fasting labs and CBCs to monitor her white blood cell count.
Covid vaccine status.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is unvaccinated against COVID-19 due to concerns about side effects however I explained that supplements are not effective in preventing COVID-19 and that vaccination is the only true preventative measure against COVID-19 given her high risk status due to quadriplegia status. I advised the patient that I would consider her at high risk if she does not get vaccinated.

Ibuprofen 800 mg daily.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The onset of her symptoms began 2 weeks ago. She reports that she has been having trouble reading and straight lines, as well as noticing that her door frames have been looking crooked to her. She also reports that she has trouble adjusting to dim lights when going out to dinner with her husband. The patient denies any history of a recent eye injury or trauma.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she smokes approximately 1 pack of cigarettes per day. She states that she has tried to stop smoking on several occasions but has been unable to completely stop.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is married and lives in Arlington, TX. She enjoys going out to dinner at McDonald’s, where she orders eggplant parmesan.

MEDICATIONS

The patient denies taking any medications at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Ears, Nose, Mouth and Throat: Denies hearing loss or ear pain.
• Eyes: Reports blurred vision, difficulty adjusting to dim lights when going out to dinner with her husband.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Ears, Nose, Mouth and Throat: Examination of the ears, nose, mouth and throat are unremarkable in appearance and extraoral examination is unremarkable in appearance.
• Eyes: Examination of the anterior segment reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. The right cornea is clear with no mVI or PCIOL cupping. The left cornea is clear with no mVII cupping or PE changes in the fovea. Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina attached 360 degrees without any tears or holes or PE changes in the fovea. Posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula thickening of the retina presence of subretinal fluid accumulation positive for hemorrhage left eye. The left cornea is clear with no mVII cupping PE changes in the fovea no hemorrhage or subretinal fluid retina is attached.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) shows drusen deposit. Retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
• Medical Reasoning: The diagnostic tests and eye exam are really indicative of neovascular age-related macular degeneration so this is advanced to a stage that usually leads to more severe vision loss and it really happens when those abnormal blood vessels start to grow beneath the retina and they will leak fluid and blood which can create a large blind spot in the center of the visual field.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I reviewed all diagnostic tests with the patient today including OCT results which show drusen deposit retinal pigment epithelium subretinal fluid accumulation choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neurovascular age related macular degeneration so this is advanced to a stage that usually leads to more severe vision loss and it really happens when those abnormal blood vessels start to grow beneath the retina and they will leak fluid and blood which can create a large blind spot in the center of the visual field.
• Medical Treatment: I recommended an injection of Lucentis once a month it’s injected into vitreous portion after it’s been numbed injections are given regularly over period time may slow rate vision decline or stop further vision loss but however disease may also progress despite treatment.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

The patient reports that she fell off of a tandem bicycle and struck her right knee on a curb approximately 2 weeks ago. She localizes her pain to the medial aspect of the knee. She also reports occasional clicking with full extension of the knee, as well as occasional instability with ambulation. The patient states that her pain is the worst when ambulating up an incline. She denies any previous right knee issues. The patient enjoys walking her dogs and swimming but has not done this since her injury.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking ibuprofen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right knee reveals medial joint line tenderness. Pes bursa is nontender. Epicondyle is nontender and soft. There are no signs of swelling or erythema. Lateral side is nontender with dry, 1/10 inch abrasions, which appear to be approximately 1 week old. Range of motion is full bilaterally without pain or stiffness.
Ligaments: Right medial collateral ligament is intact and valgus stable. Right lateral collateral ligament is intact and valgus stable. There is mild laxity in the posterior drawer bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

4 views of the right knee were obtained today, which have been reviewed in office today.
X-rays reveal no evidence of fracture or bone spurs, but there appears to be some posterior subluxation of the tibia.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee pain.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient sustained a traumatic injury to her right knee when she fell off a tandem bicycle and struck her right knee on a curb approximately 2 weeks ago. Her symptoms are consistent with a possible posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) sprain.
• Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options for her current symptoms, including bracing, physical therapy, and possibly surgery if necessary.
• Medical Treatment: We will start with bracing today and I will refer her to physical therapy for close monitoring at home or near work.
• Additional Testing: We will order an MRI to evaluate for any additional injuries such as meniscal tears or cartilage damage.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Right elbow pain.

Zachary Wood is a pleasant 45-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Karen Allen is a 34-year-old female with a history of chronic migraines and hypertension who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of abdominal pain. The onset of her abdominal pain began 10 days ago with mild discomfort on the right side, which has progressively worsened over the last couple of days. She rates her pain as a 4 or 5 out of 10, but it can reach as high as a 7 or 8. The pain is usually worse after meals, but it is not too bad in the morning before eating. She denies any radiating pain to the left side. She has had some nausea and heartburn, but no vomiting. The patient states that her abdomen is tender to palpation and certain positions make it worse when she is most tender. She denies any urinary symptoms or blood in her urine. She also denies any diarrhea or blood in her stool.

The patient reports that she has not been hungry lately due to nausea and feels fatigued over the last week.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she traveled to Europe last summer.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she does not watch the Super Bowl when it is on because she does not eat junk food when she watches TV.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she takes Excedrin Migraine as needed for treatment of migraines, Sumatriptan as needed for breakthrough migraine pain, and Lisinopril 20 mg per day for hypertension.
note.objective_exam:

CV: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior exam.

- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed alternative explanations for her symptoms including gallstones and possible infection in her gallbladder.
- Medical Treatment: We will order blood tests and an ultrasound today to evaluate for gallstones or infection in her gallbladder.
- Additional Testing: CBC chem12 urinalysis pregnancy test will be ordered today.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that she has had rare migraines recently but they are responsive to Excedrin Migraine at home and Sumatriptan when needed at home if Excedrin Migraine does not respond.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed lifestyle modifications including avoiding alcohol binges and caffeine binges, getting enough sleep, etc., which seem to be helpful at this time.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Excedrin Migraine as needed over-the-counter for treatment; Sumatriptan as needed for breakthrough migraine pain; avoid alcohol binges and caffeine binges; try to get enough sleep at night.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Rogers is a pleasant 50-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left shoulder pain. The onset of her pain began 2 weeks ago. She denies any previous trauma or injury to her left shoulder. She is very active and has been renovating her basement recently. The patient states that she has been doing a lot with that, but she does not remember hitting her shoulder or doing anything that would cause the pain.

The patient reports that she is able to move her left arm for me, but she has a lot of pain when she tries to reach for something or lift anything. She states that she does not even try to raise her arm over her head because it really hurts. The patient reports that she has constant pain in her left shoulder and it is always there, but when she sleeps on her left side, the pain goes up. She states that she cannot lay on her left side at all.

The patient reports that without Tylenol, her pain level is a 3 out of 10. With Tylenol, it goes down to a 2 or 3 out of 10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the arm or hand.
note.objective_exam:

MSK: Examination of the Left Shoulder
- Active ROM: Limited range of motion bilaterally due to pain.
- Passive ROM: Limited range of motion bilaterally due to pain.
- Palpation: Tenderness over the greater tuberosity of the humerus without tenderness at the sternoclavicular or clavicular joints.
- Neurovascular integrity: Cap refill is brisk in less than 3 seconds bilaterally. Motor strength and sensation are intact to light touch bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray imaging of the left shoulder was obtained today and reviewed in office today. There are no fractures or bony abnormalities present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Left Shoulder Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with the patient that we will start with conservative management with physical therapy for approximately 6-8 weeks and continue taking Tylenol PRN if symptoms do not improve. We will then consider steroid injection if necessary.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an MRI of the left shoulder for further evaluation.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a pleasant male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began yesterday when he was playing basketball for the first time in 2 years. He states that he went up for a rebound and came down and felt like his knee popped. He describes his pain as achy, located on the medial aspect of his right knee. He notes that he can bear weight on his right leg but is favoring it. His pain level is approximately 4/10.

The patient reports that he has been taking Tylenol for pain, which has provided some relief but not much.

The patient denies any history of trauma to the right knee.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he plays basketball for the first time in 2 years.

MEDICAL HISTORY

The patient reports a history of hypertension and diabetes.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Norvasc 5 mg daily; Metformin 500 mg daily; Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any neurological symptoms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi are present.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur is heard at the left sternal border. This has been present for several years and is not concerning at this time.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals tenderness to palpation over the medial aspect of the knee. There is some edema and ecchymosis present. Varus and valgus testing are negative. Range of motion is slightly painful with bending and straightening, but full range of motion is maintained.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray of the right knee was obtained today in office and revealed no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right Knee MCL Strain/MCL Tear: The patient presents today with right knee pain after playing basketball for the first time in 2 years. Examination reveals tenderness to palpation over the medial aspect of the knee, edema, ecchymosis, and a negative varus and valgus test. X-ray was unremarkable revealing no evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities. We had an MRI performed today which will be reviewed in follow-up today.
- Medical Reasoning: The clinical presentation is consistent with an MCL strain or tear given her examination findings today as well as her x-ray results which were unremarkable.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed treatment options with the patient today including continued use of Tylenol for pain management as well as meloxicam 15 mg once daily for swelling reduction. We also discussed placing her in a knee immobilizer for 2 weeks to allow her to rest her right knee completely until we can get her MRI results back.
- Medical Treatment: Continue Tylenol as needed for pain management only; prescribe Meloxicam 15 mg once daily; place patient in a right ankle immobilizer for 2 weeks until MRI results are available.
2. Diabetes Type 2: The patient presents today with elevated blood sugar levels at home which are consistent with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus type 2 at this point in time due to non-adherence with medication regimen including Metformin due to gastrointestinal upset.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated and fluctuating blood pressures.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Robert Harris is a 67-year-old male with a history of essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis who presents today for evaluation of elevated and fluctuating blood pressures. The patient reports that his blood pressure has been well controlled over the last 3 to 4 weeks, but he has experienced periods of lightheadedness, slight headache, and elevated blood pressure readings. He notes that he has checked his blood pressure when he felt lightheaded and it was high at those times. The patient denies passing out or chest pain or trouble breathing. He also denies headaches or neurologic symptoms such as numbness, weakness, balance instability, or anything like that. The patient states that he is still taking lisinopril 20 mg twice per day and denies missing doses.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he enjoys playing golf.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is currently taking lisinopril 20 mg twice per day, atorvastatin, and occasional Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or dyspnea on exertion.
• Neurological: Denies headaches or neurologic symptoms such as numbness, weakness, balance instability.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports mild pain in the knees.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior examination. No murmurs heard at the apex. No gallops or rales heard at the lung bases. No wheezes or rhonchi heard. Excellent air movement bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Elevated Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure has been fluctuating over the past few weeks with episodes of lightheadedness and elevated blood pressure readings. His current medication regimen is not adequate to control his blood pressure.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including increasing fluid intake to stay hydrated when it warms up as well as limiting alcohol consumption to no more than 2 drinks per week.
- Medical Treatment: I am going to increase his lisinopril to 60 mg twice per day and add hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once per day. I want him to check his blood pressure measurements twice a day for the next two weeks then let's see him back in two weeks to check on how he's doing.
2. Hyperlipidemia.
- Medical Reasoning: His current medication regimen is adequate for managing his hyperlipidemia.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including increasing fluid intake to stay hydrated when it warms up as well as limiting alcohol consumption to no more than 2 drinks per week.
- Medical Treatment: Continue with atorvastatin indefinitely. Send cholesterol panel CBC with differential comprehensive metabolic panel urinalysis for kidney function testing.
