note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Billy Wright is a pleasant 74-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a cough. The patient reports that he started coughing about a week ago. He states that he has been bringing up some yellow stuff and not feeling well over the last 2 days. The patient denies fevers, chills, shortness of breath, runny nose, sore throat, sinus pressure or pressure in his sinuses.

The patient reports that he twisted his right knee when he was coughing and fell down the stairs. He states that he has been able to walk since that happened but it hurts mostly on the inside. The patient denies limping at this time but does have a little bit of a limp. He denies taking any pain medication for his knee pain.

The patient reports that he is not watching his salt intake and does not take his blood sugars either.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that he has a history of hypertension and diabetes.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient works as a teacher. He is married and lives on the other side of town from his wife.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he is taking lisinopril 20 mg daily and metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Respiratory: Examination of the face reveals pain to palpation over bilateral maxillary sinuses. Examination of the nose reveals erythema and edema of the nasal turbinates bilaterally with associated yellow discharge. Examination of the throat reveals no erythema or edema or exudate in the peritonsillar space. Examination of the neck reveals bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Examination of the lungs reveals coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clears with cough.
• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals pain to palpation. There is decreased flexion and extension of the right knee with associated ecchymosis to the right medial knee. No effusion is present.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Cough.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of a cough which began approximately 1 week ago. His symptoms have worsened over the last 2 days with productive coughing up yellow sputum.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him today that I believe this is likely viral in nature at this time but we will monitor him closely for any signs or symptoms suggesting pneumonia.
- Medical Treatment: I recommended supportive care including guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to help cough up phlegm without antibiotics at this time but if symptoms worsen we will consider ordering a chest x-ray.
• Right Knee Pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of right knee pain which began after he twisted his knee when he was coughing and fell down stairs this morning. He denies limping at this time but does have some discomfort on ambulation.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him today that I believe this is likely an LCL strain from his fall this morning but we will order an x-ray to rule out any bony injury.
- Medical Treatment: We will refer him to physical therapy to strengthen those muscles around his right knee area and prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain control.
• Hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood pressure was elevated at 125/62 mmHg in office today which is consistent with his history of hypertension.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed lifestyle modifications including dietary changes which should help manage blood pressure levels going forward as well as regular monitoring at home using home blood pressure monitoring devices as prescribed by me today.
- Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 20 mg once daily as prescribed by me today, order lipid panel due to elevated blood pressure.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

High blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Theresa Rodriguez is a pleasant 41-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of high blood pressure. She has been taking chlorthalidone for hypertension for a long time, but she has been having stomachaches from this medication. She denies adhering to her medication regimen as she forgets to take it. She reports that she has been experiencing headaches for about a month, which are throbbing in nature and come and go. These headaches are associated with dizziness and blurry vision. The patient reports chest pain or shortness of breath when she experiences these headaches.

The patient states that she has been taking Tylenol for her headaches, which helps a little bit. She denies any other symptoms such as nausea or vomiting.

The patient reports that she is not adhering to her medication regimen as she forgets to take it. She states that she probably takes her metformin every other day.

PAST HISTORY

The patient reports that she has had high blood pressure for a long time.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

The patient is currently taking chlorthalidone and metformin.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
• Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain or shortness of breath on exertion.
• Neurological: Reports headache, dizziness, blurry vision.
• Respiratory: Denies dyspnea on exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Constitutional: Normal vital signs except elevated blood pressure (172/98). Oxygenation is within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Uncontrolled hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's elevated blood pressure is multifactorial in nature and may be related to her diet and non-adherence with her current medication regimen. We will need to discuss dietary changes with the patient today and also consider changing her current medication regimen if necessary.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I encouraged the patient to continue taking her current medication regimen today and advised her to take it every day by setting a reminder on her iPhone. I also recommended that we monitor her blood pressure 3 times per week at home using a home blood pressure monitor. I explained the importance of reducing sodium intake in her diet and recommended that we schedule a nutritionist visit for further guidance on dietary changes.
- Medical Treatment: Continue chlorthalidone daily as prescribed. Increase metformin dose to 1500 mg daily as prescribed. Monitor blood sugar levels regularly while on this new dose of metformin.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

The patient reports that this is the first time she has experienced right shoulder pain.

The patient reports that she has been remodeling her house.

Negative for any family history of musculoskeletal issues.

The patient reports that she has been taking Advil for her pain.

Musculoskeletal: Reports right shoulder pain, numbness, tingling in the right arm and hand.

• Neurological: Brisk capillary refill of less than 3 seconds bilaterally. Equal and bilateral response to sensation and touch.
note.objective_results:

note.assessment_and_plan:

• Right shoulder rotator cuff tendinopathy.

• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Vision changes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Thomas is a pleasant 65-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of vision changes. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 3 to 4 months ago. He reports that he has trouble adjusting in dark environments, particularly when reading. He also notes that straight lines appear wavy to him, which he attributes to the paneling in his office. He denies any improvement in his symptoms.

The patient and his wife dine out almost every night and he believes this may be contributing to his vision problems. He denies any improvement in his symptoms.

The patient has a history of smoking 1 pack per day and reports that he has tried various methods to quit including hypnosis, lozenges, and chewing gum. He admits that he will often go out for a cigarette without his wife and then purchase one from someone else.

PAST HISTORY

History of high blood pressure.
Smoking history: 1 pack per day.

MEDICATIONS

Blood pressure medication.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies weight loss or gain.
Eyes: Reports vision changes, difficulty adjusting in dark environments, straight lines appear wavy to him.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Eyes: Examination of the anterior segment reveals clear corneas bilaterally with no signs of nVIta or peak hole cupping. The fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina attached 360 degrees with no holes or tears noted. RPE changes are present in the fovea. Drusen are present in the macula bilaterally with retinal thickening and subretinal fluid accumulation and exudate accumulation present bilaterally. It is positive for hemorrhage bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Diagnostic exam reveals drusen deposits under the RPE which is the retinal pigment epithelium and subretinal fluid so SRF accumulation and choroidal neovascular membrane can also be visualized in that test.
Fluorescein angiography reveals focal area of leakage consistent with neurovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Matthew Thomas is a pleasant 65-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of vision changes.
Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (wet macular degeneration) is diagnosed based on diagnostic exam findings as well as fluorescein angiography results today.
INSTRUCTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS IN LIGHT OF THE EXAMINATION AND IMAGING FINDINGS TODAY, I have discussed treatment options with the patient today including Lucentis injections once per month into the vitreous portion of the eye after numbing the eye so he will not feel any pain during injection at all. The patient understands and agrees with this plan in full.
The patient will follow up with me once a month for injections.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up on neo-adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III nonsmall cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents for a follow-up appointment on her neo-adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III nonsmall cell lung cancer. The patient reports that she has been doing well, but she has noticed some shortness of breath over the weekend. She states that she was previously active and would take her dog for mile-long walks every day, but now she can only walk down the street without being short of breath. The patient denies coughing or phlegm. She also denies fever. The patient reports that she has a dry cough, which hurts when she swallows. She states that the food is not getting stuck when she swallows, but it just hurts. The patient denies dysphagia with solids or liquids. She states that she has been taking Ensure and milkshakes to help with hydration.

The patient reports that her mental status is stable today. She states that she is devastated by her diagnosis and is trying to figure everything out. She reports that her husband and daughter have been very helpful with her emotional support.

The patient reports that her nausea and fatigue have improved since starting chemotherapy, but she was a little nauseated and tired after her last dose of cisplatin and etoposide. She states that Zofran helped with the nausea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, chills.
• Respiratory: Denies coughing or phlegm.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports dry cough, dysphagia with swallowing.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies body aches.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Lungs: Bilateral crackles present at auscultation; this could be due to fluid in the lungs due to lung cancer diagnosis.
Skin: Erythema on the anterior aspect of the chest on the left side; this could be due to radiation burn which will improve once treatment is completed.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pathology report shows evidence of a 4.4 cm left upper lobe nodule.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Stage III nonsmall cell lung cancer in progress.
- Continue neo-adjuvant chemotherapy regimen as prescribed today.
- Continue radiation therapy at 45 Gy as prescribed today until completion of chemotherapy regimen at which point we will proceed with additional testing in hopes of resecting tumor which has decreased in size slightly since last imaging studies were obtained.
2. Radiation pneumonitis in progress.
- Prescribe low dose steroid prednisone 40 mg once daily for 5 days to reduce inflammation in lungs and improve breathing symptoms.
The patient has never been on steroids before and will likely not experience significant side effects from this treatment plan given its short duration (5 days). We will monitor for any side effects such as muscle aches after discontinuation of prednisone treatment plan.
3. Dysphagia due to radiation pneumonitis in progress.
- Prescribe lidocaine lozenges 4 times daily to help alleviate pain associated with swallowing.

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents for a follow-up appointment on her neo-adjuvant chemotherapy for stage III nonsmall cell lung cancer. The patient reports that she has been doing well, but she has noticed some shortness of breath over the weekend. She states that she was previously active and would take her dog for mile-long walks every day, but now she can only walk down the street without being short of breath. The patient denies coughing or phlegm. She also denies fever. The patient reports that she has a dry cough, which hurts when she swallows. She states that the food is not getting stuck when she swallows, but it just hurts. The patient denies dysphagia with solids or liquids. She states that she has been taking Ensure and milkshakes to help with hydration.

The patient reports that her mental status is stable today. She states that she is devastated by her diagnosis and is trying to figure everything out. She reports that her husband and daughter have been very helpful with her emotional support.

The patient reports that her nausea and fatigue have improved since starting chemotherapy, but she was a little nauseated and tired after her last dose of cisplatin and etoposide. She states that Zofran helped with the nausea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever, chills.
• Respiratory: Denies coughing or phlegm.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports dry cough, dysphagia with swallowing.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies body aches.
model_note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Lungs: Bilateral crackles present at auscultation; this could be due to fluid in the lungs due to lung cancer diagnosis.
Skin: Erythema on the anterior aspect of the chest on the left side; this could be due to radiation burn which will improve once treatment is completed.
model_note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pathology report shows evidence of a 4.4 cm left upper lobe nodule.
model_note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Stage III nonsmall cell lung cancer in progress.
- Continue neo-adjuvant chemotherapy regimen as prescribed today.
- Continue radiation therapy at 45 Gy as prescribed today until completion of chemotherapy regimen at which point we will proceed with additional testing in hopes of resecting tumor which has decreased in size slightly since last imaging studies were obtained.
2. Radiation pneumonitis in progress.
- Prescribe low dose steroid prednisone 40 mg once daily for 5 days to reduce inflammation in lungs and improve breathing symptoms.
The patient has never been on steroids before and will likely not experience significant side effects from this treatment plan given its short duration (5 days). We will monitor for any side effects such as muscle aches after discontinuation of prednisone treatment plan.
3. Dysphagia due to radiation pneumonitis in progress.
- Prescribe lidocaine lozenges 4 times daily to help alleviate pain associated with swallowing.

Kidney stone.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of a kidney stone. The patient reports that he has been experiencing right flank pain radiating down to his groin for the past 2 weeks. The pain is intermittent and is worse with increased fluid intake and physical activity. He denies any hematuria or dysuria. The patient states that he has had previous episodes of kidney stones, some of which he has passed on his own within a week, while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy. He notes that his family members have also had kidney stones in the past.

• Constitutional: Denies fevers, chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports right flank pain.
• Genitourinary: Denies hematuria, dysuria.
note.objective_exam:

• Cardiovascular: Blood pressure is slightly elevated.
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT scan of the right flank was reviewed today, 05/06/2022. It revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joshua Reyes is an 18-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of a kidney stone.

Medical Reasoning:
The patient's symptoms are consistent with a kidney stone. His history of previous episodes of kidney stones supports this diagnosis as well as his family history of kidney stones.
Patient Education and Counseling:
The patient was counseled on conservative management options including increasing fluid intake and using a strainer when urinating. He was also advised on alternative pain management options including tramadol if needed.
Medical Treatment:
The patient will continue to increase fluid intake and use a strainer when urinating at home. He will be prescribed tramadol 50 mg as needed for pain control if necessary due to increased pain over the weekend. A BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture will be ordered to evaluate for infection or other urinary tract issues.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Frank Lee is a pleasant 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago. He states that he has been having shortness of breath for about 6 months prior to this, and he was treated with an increase in his Lasix dose at that time and he seemed to get better.

The patient reports that he has been watching his salt intake, but admits that it has been the holidays the last couple of weeks and he believes that his diet has not been everything it should have been. He denies any swelling in his legs. He states that he takes Lasix every day as prescribed. He denies any decrease in urination recently, but does report urinating at night 1-2 times per night.

The patient reports that he feels short of breath when walking around stairs in particular when walking quickly. He also reports that he goes from one pillow to two pillows at night. He denies waking up really short of breath, however, this did occur 6 months ago.

The patient last saw his nephrologist approximately 1 month ago. The patient denies taking Motrin or Advil due to knee pain, however, he did take Motrin for a while and stopped as quickly as possible after experiencing some pain in his feet.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of coronary disease, acute myocardial infarction in 2018, placement of a coronary artery stent in the right coronary artery in 2018, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient is a basketball fan.
